Three Checks Before You Book A watch that doesn't last the day isn't always a battery fault. These checks help you tell. Look at Battery Health. On the watch, open Settings, then Battery, then Battery Health. Maximum Capacity shows how much of the original capacity is left. If it says "Service", the battery is worn out. Rule out your settings. Apple's own guide to an Apple Watch battery that drains too quickly lists the main drains: Always On display, cellular use away from your iPhone, weak signal, and GPS and heart-rate readings during outdoor workouts. If changing these fixes your battery life, you don't need a repair. Watch for the urgent signs. If the watch shuts down at 30 to 50%, won't switch on even on its charger, or the screen has started lifting away from the case, stop wearing it. A lifting screen usually means the battery has swollen, and you should bring it in quickly. Not sure which of these you have? Long Days at Melrose Arch Are Hard on an Old Battery Melrose Arch isn't a mall. It's a mixed-use precinct between Rosebank and Sandton, with direct access to the M1 and pedestrian-first cobbled streets. Offices, apartments and shops sit around the Piazza and Melrose Square, and the precinct is owned by the Amdec Group. It also has four hotels with more than 700 rooms between them, including the Marriott, African Pride and Protea Fire & Ice! hotels. So the people whose iPhones run flat here are a mix: office workers in the blue-chip tenancies, residents, and visitors in town for a few days. A typical day here is hard on a tired battery. You park underground, sit through back-to-back video calls, hotspot a laptop when the office Wi-Fi drops, then follow your map app onto the M1 at five o'clock. A healthy battery copes with that. One that's down to 80% capacity or less starts shutting down at 25%, dimming the screen or slowing the phone. You usually notice when you need the phone most, like paying for parking or approving a banking login. We don't have a branch at Melrose Arch. Our workshop is in Silvamonte, a short drive east, and every battery replacement is done there. What Drains an iPhone Around the Precinct Not every flat battery is a worn battery. This table shows how a normal Melrose Arch day affects a healthy battery compared with a worn one, so you can tell which one you have. Where you are Why it uses power Healthy battery Worn battery Underground parking and inner offices Weak signal makes the phone search for a network Drains faster, recovers outside Drops fast, or shuts down with charge showing Video calls and hotspotting a laptop Screen, camera, radio and processor all working at once Warm, steady drain Sudden jumps in percentage, hot to the touch Navigation on the M1 or Corlett Drive GPS, a bright screen and mobile data together Lasts the drive Needs a car charger to survive the trip A full day as a hotel guest or visitor Boarding passes, maps, bookings and photos, far from your charger Gets you to the evening Dead by mid-afternoon Check Settings > Battery > Battery Health (on newer iOS versions, Battery Health & Charging ). If Maximum Capacity is around 80% or lower, or you see a "Service" message, the battery is worn. Apple explains how this works, including why an ageing battery slows the phone down, in its guide to iPhone battery and performance . Battery, Charging Port or Something Deeper? A phone that won't last the day can also be a charging fault. A lint-packed port at the end of a long week can look exactly like a dead battery. So can a damaged charging chip, or a phone that keeps restarting on its own. These are the related repairs we check for in the same free diagnostic: Charging port repair (from R550): charges only at an angle, cable falls out, or "Accessory not supported". Charging IC repair (assessment + quote): no charging at all, or the percentage sticks even though the cable and port are fine. Restart loop repair (assessment + quote): the phone restarts every few minutes. Sometimes it's a failing battery, sometimes a sensor flex. We read the panic log to find out which. Logic board repair (assessment + quote): board-level faults found under the microscope after the simpler causes are ruled out. If a new battery isn't the fix, we tell you before you pay for one. It opened at the end of 1992 as Linksfield Park Clinic, and Netcare bought it in 1997. Today it runs an accredited Level 3 emergency department, cardiology, renal dialysis, robotic-assisted orthopaedic surgery and a cochlear implant service, according to Netcare's own 30-year history of the hospital . A hospital is where a weak iPhone speaker lets you down at the worst moment. Picture a family member pacing the corridor outside a ward, phone pressed to their ear, catching every second word from the doctor. Our workshop is in Silvamonte, a short drive north, and every speaker repair is done there. Earpiece or Loudspeaker? How to Tell Which One Failed Your iPhone has two speakers, and they fail in different ways. The earpiece (top speaker) is the one you hear calls through when the phone is at your ear. The loudspeaker (bottom speaker) plays ringtones, alarms, speakerphone calls and videos. On iPhones with Face ID, they also work together for stereo sound. A quick test: play some music and cover the bottom edge of the phone, then the top. If one end is much quieter, distorted or silent, that's the speaker at fault. If calls only fail when the phone is at your ear but speakerphone is fine, it's the earpiece. Over months, damp wipes and sanitiser gel on your hands leave a film in the fine mesh, and lint from coat and scrub pockets sticks to it. The result is a speaker that slowly gets quieter. It often isn't broken at all. That's why we always clean the mesh and test again before we suggest a new part. If cleaning brings the volume back, you pay nothing for a replacement you don't need. To keep it that way, wipe the phone with the wipe wrung out, keep the grilles facing down, and let it dry before it goes back in your pocket. View all service areas → Apple Watch Series 1/2/3 — frequently asked questions My older Apple Watch screen is lifting — fixable? Yes — and it's important you bring it in immediately. The lifting screen means the battery has swollen, which is a fire and chemical hazard. We safely remove and dispose of the swollen cell, fit a new battery, and reseal the case. Pricing is R900 — no extra charge for swollen battery handling. Stop wearing it until we've handled it. Is it worth repairing my Series 3 (or older) Apple Watch? Honest answer: depends on the fault. Single battery replacement at R900 is worth it for sentimental value or as a basic fitness tracker. Multiple faults reaching R2,000+ usually isn't economical. Swollen battery cases we always recommend repairing immediately for safety, even if you don't plan to use the watch — to make safe disposal possible. Will my Series 3 still pair to my iPhone after repair? Yes — but Series 3 is no longer supported by current iOS Watch app. You'll need to keep the existing pairing intact. If your watch needs full restore (lost pairing), pairing back to current iPhones may not be possible due to software incompatibility. We confirm during diagnostic if this risk applies to your specific repair. Are parts still available for Series 1, 2, and 3? Limited but available for most common services. Batteries, screens, and charging components remain stocked. Some specialty parts have longer lead times or aren't available. We confirm parts availability when sending your quote. Does my older Apple Watch still get software updates? No — Apple has ended watchOS support for Series 1, 2, and 3. Your watch continues working with its last installed watchOS but won't receive feature or security updates going forward. App developers are increasingly dropping support for older watchOS versions, so functionality will gradually reduce over time. Can my older Apple Watch be turned into a fitness tracker only? Yes — even without active iPhone pairing or new watchOS, the watch can still track workouts, heart rate, and steps locally. After repair we can set it up in standalone mode for basic fitness tracking. This is a good option for a working older watch you don't need notifications on. Will my repaired Series 3 still be water resistant? Honest answer: Series 1/2/3 seals are 8-10 years old and any opened Apple Watch has reduced water resistance vs factory new. We use cold-press resealing to restore as much as practically possible. Splashes and rain are fine. We strongly recommend treating older repaired watches as splash-resistant only — no swimming, hot tubs, or steam rooms. How long does older Apple Watch repair take? Most Series 1/2/3 repairs are 24-48 hours. Swollen battery cases get same-day priority queue position for safety reasons. Battery and Crown work usually same-day in Gauteng walk-ins. Limited-stock parts may add 2-3 days. Nationwide via The Courier Guy: 2-3 days door-to-door on overnight. Few have the microscope, the cold-press resealing equipment, the OEM-grade parts catalogue, or the years of practice it takes to actually repair a bonded-screen Apple Watch and put it back together properly. Here's what that means in practice. Diagnosis under a microscope Apple Watch components are tiny — the bonded OLED, the Force Touch cable, the Digital Crown switch, the heart-sensor flex. We examine every Watch under a stereo microscope to identify the exact failed component rather than guessing at "the screen" or "the board." The failed part named in your quote Your written quote tells you exactly what's wrong. "OLED display assembly, Series 7 41mm" not "screen issue." "Digital Crown switch contamination" not "Crown problem." You agree to fix a specific named fault, not a vague verdict. Repaired and resealed, not replaced iStore quotes R7,000-R18,000 to replace an Apple Watch. We repair yours for R900-R3,500 in most cases, and your original Watch — with all its activity rings, sleep data, ECG history, and pairing — stays exactly as it was. Every Watch gets professional cold-press adhesive resealing before it leaves the workshop. Honest verdicts, including "walk away" When a repair doesn't make sense — a Series 3 needing both screen and battery, a heavily-corroded older SE — we say so before any work begins. Sometimes replacement is the right answer. We'd rather tell you that than pad an invoice. Apple Watch battery lifespan guide Apple Watch batteries are smaller than iPad or MacBook batteries and work much harder — always-on display, GPS workouts, sleep tracking, and continuous heart-rate monitoring all draw current 24 hours a day. Apple rates them to retain 80% of original capacity at 1,000 cycles, but real-world performance varies significantly by series and usage intensity. Apple Watch Ultra Ultra · Ultra 2 · Ultra 3 500 Cycles · Monitor 700 Cycles · Replace Typical lifespan: 4–5 years. Ultra models have larger batteries (up to 36 hours runtime) but are typically used heavily — multi-day hikes, long GPS workouts, dive sessions. Heavy GPS and cellular use accelerates cycle wear. Below 80% capacity, expect runtime to drop from 36 hours to 18–20 hours. Apple Watch Series 7-11 Series 7 · 8 · 9 · 10 · 11 400 Cycles · Monitor 600 Cycles · Replace Typical lifespan: 3–4 years. Mainstream Apple Watch Series with always-on display draws meaningful current. Most users see noticeable battery drop-off after 2.5–3 years. Below 80% capacity you'll struggle to make it through a full day with workout tracking. Battery replacement restores all-day runtime. SE & Series 4-6 SE · SE 2 · SE 3 · Series 4-6 350 Cycles · Monitor 500 Cycles · Replace Typical lifespan: 3–4 years. SE and older Series have smaller batteries that hit the wear threshold faster. Watch out for swollen batteries on Series 4–6 — these can lift the screen off the case. If your screen is starting to detach, stop wearing it and bring it in. Replacement is cost-effective on these models. Series 1 · 2 · 3 Original through Series 3 7+ Years old Any Swelling · Replace Vintage territory. Original batteries on these models are well past their service life and are the most likely to swell. A swollen battery is a fire risk and will eventually push the screen off. Replace any visibly swollen battery immediately. watchOS support for these models has ended — replacement is feasible but the machine is on borrowed time. How to check your Apple Watch battery health: On your iPhone, open the Watch app → My Watch → General → About → Battery. Or directly on your Watch: Settings → Battery → Battery Health. If Maximum Capacity is below 80% or runtime has dropped noticeably, WhatsApp us for a battery replacement quote — same-day service available. Known Apple Watch issues Every Apple Watch generation eventually develops a personality — usually expressed through a specific design fault that turns up like clockwork after a few years of use. Below are the ones we see most often on the workshop bench. None is terminal. Each has a well-defined repair path and we've handled all of them many times over. Most common · All series with age Swollen battery — screen lift The most common Apple Watch fault we see. Battery cells expand with age and push the display assembly up and out of the case — first a small gap at the edge, then the screen lifts visibly. The Series 0-3 era is most affected (Apple ran an extended service programme that has now ended) but it happens on Series 4-6 frequently and on later models with age. A swollen lithium-polymer cell is a fire risk. Stop wearing the Watch immediately. iAssist fix: Safe removal and disposal of the swollen cell, new OEM-grade battery fitted, cold-press resealing to restore water resistance. 6-month warranty on the replacement. Series 4 · 5 · 6 · 7 · SE · SE 2 Digital Crown corrosion & sweat damage Sweat, sunscreen, and salt water build up around the Digital Crown over time, particularly on Watches used during workouts or swimming. The Crown gets stuck, scrolls erratically when nothing is touching it, or stops registering presses. Heavy fitness use accelerates the failure. Prevention tip: rinse your Apple Watch under fresh water after sweaty workouts or swimming. iAssist fix: Crown disassembly, deep ultrasonic clean, and re-lubrication. Where the internal switch has corroded, full Crown assembly replacement. Series 4 onwards · all back-glass models Heart rate & sensor failures The back-glass sensor array on Series 4 onwards houses the heart rate sensor, ECG electrodes, and blood-oxygen sensor on newer models. Cracks in the back glass, sweat ingress around the sensor edges, or impact damage can disable these sensors — sometimes silently, with the Watch reporting "couldn't measure" or unrealistic heart-rate readings. Apple replaces the whole Watch for this fault. We repair it. iAssist fix: Back-glass replacement with sensor calibration. Sensor function tested before the Watch leaves the workshop. Apple Watch Ultra · Ultra 2 · Ultra 3 Action Button sticking The Ultra series added a customisable Action Button on the left side of the case — a useful addition that's also a new ingress point. Hard hits, sweat, sand (the Ultra is marketed as an outdoor/dive Watch), and pressure-washing can all cause the Action Button to stick down or stop registering presses. Customers often only notice when their assigned action — a workout shortcut, dive mode, torch — fails to trigger. iAssist fix: Action Button assembly disassembly, deep clean, switch replacement where needed. Cold-press resealing afterwards to restore Ultra's marine rating as closely as possible. Free Apple Watch diagnostics on all models. Written fixed-price quote before any work begins. No hidden fees. Apple Watches use precision adhesive seals to maintain water resistance. The screen, back glass, side button, Crown, and speaker grille all rely on these seals. Once a Watch is opened — for any reason — the seals are broken and water resistance is significantly reduced. To restore resistance properly, you need three things: new factory-spec adhesive gaskets, the right adhesive type for each location, and most importantly cold-press equipment that applies precise pressure across the case while the adhesive cures. This is the equipment most independent repair shops do not have. They use double-sided tape, glue dots, or generic adhesive — none of which restore meaningful water resistance. When you need cold-press resealing Watch was repaired elsewhere Previous shop opened the case but did not properly reseal. Common when the price was suspiciously low. DIY repair attempted You opened the Watch yourself or a friend did. Cold-press equipment is needed to properly restore the seal — household tools cannot achieve it. Visible seal lift Screen edge has lifted slightly, or you can see the bond line is gappy. Adhesive failure — needs full reseal. Aged seal failure Watch is 4+ years old, never repaired, but you can see condensation or fogging under the screen. Original seal degraded. Crown / button gasket failure Specific gasket around the Crown or button has failed. We can replace just that gasket without full Watch resealing. Pre-emptive sealing Going on a beach or pool holiday and worried about an aging Watch — we can pre-emptively reseal to restore resistance before exposure. Series 4/5 is R550. Series 6, SE, and SE 2 are R600. Series 7/8/9 is R700. Series 10 and SE 3 are R800. Series 11 is R850. Apple Watch Ultra (all generations) is R900. We confirm exact pricing after free diagnostic. Why has my Apple Watch speaker stopped working? Three common causes: sweat and dust blockage of the speaker grille (cleanable, cheapest), liquid damage to the speaker driver (replacement needed), or aged speaker module failure (replacement needed). We diagnose which one before quoting — sometimes a deep clean resolves it without replacement. Why can't Siri hear me anymore? Mic membrane is most likely blocked or damaged. Sweat residue is the #1 cause — sweat dries on the mic grille and reduces sensitivity. If cleaning does not restore it, the mic module itself has failed and needs replacement. Most speaker and mic repairs are completed within 24–48 hours. For nationwide repairs via The Courier Guy, total turnaround is 2–3 working days door-to-door on overnight service, 5–7 working days on standard. Can sweat damage really affect the speaker? Yes, significantly. The speaker grille is at the lowest point of the watch case — sweat pools there during workouts and dries leaving residue. Over years this builds up and dampens sound. Heavy fitness users see speaker degradation much sooner than office workers. Do you offer a warranty on speaker / mic repairs? Yes — all Apple Watch speaker and mic repairs at iAssist are covered by a 6-month warranty on parts and labour. If the audio fault recurs within six months, we fix it at no charge. Most common cause is sweat ingress around the Action Button gasket — sweat dries inside the mechanism and corrodes the contact, or the gasket itself fails leading to liquid in the button shaft. Action Button replacement with new gasket is R1,500 and includes the standard side button — if both have failed it's covered in one repair. Is it worth replacing my Ultra 2 battery? Yes for most users. R1,800 to restore your Ultra 2 to 36-hour runtime is a strong value vs replacing the watch itself (Ultra 2 retail R20,000+). Battery replacement extends your watch's useful life by another 2-3 years. We confirm if your specific case is economical during free diagnostic. My Ultra 2 won't pair after a battery replacement somewhere else — can you fix it? Probably yes. Pairing failure post-repair is usually either incomplete reset/restore by the previous shop, or the battery health calibration wasn't refreshed. We can perform full DFU recovery and re-pair the watch. How does Ultra 2 battery wear compare to Series 9? Ultra 2 has a much larger battery (36hr vs 18hr nominal) so absolute capacity is higher, but cycle wear is similar. Heavy GPS use during workouts wears the cell faster than passive wear — Ultra 2 owners who do multi-day hikes or long workouts see meaningful capacity loss within 18-24 months. Can you fix double-tap if it's stopped working? Yes — first we test whether it's a software issue (Tier 1 watchOS reset usually fixes), then a sensor-level fault (rare), then chip-level (logic board repair). Honest answer: any opened Apple Watch has reduced water resistance vs factory new. How liquid damage actually happens to Apple Watches Apple Watches are water resistant, not waterproof. Salt water, sunscreen, soap residue, and pressure cycling all break down the gaskets over time. Common scenarios we see weekly: Hot tubs and steam rooms. Hot pressurised steam penetrates seals more easily than swimming-pool water. This is the #1 silent killer of Apple Watches. Salt water exposure. Sea water is corrosive — even one ocean swim with degraded seals can introduce enough salt to start a corrosion chain. Hot showers. Soap and shampoo residue combined with steam — both compromise seals over time. Aged seal failure. Watches 3+ years old with no obvious water exposure can develop liquid damage as the original adhesive seal degrades naturally. Post-repair seal failure. If your Watch was repaired by a shop that doesn't cold-press reseal properly, water resistance is significantly reduced. Crown / button gasket failure. Liquid often enters around the Digital Crown or side button — these gaskets fail first on heavy fitness users. Most controllers measure stick position with tiny sensors that have a contact rubbing along a track. Over time that track wears, dust gets in, and the reading wanders. Recalibrating or blowing air into the stick can help for a while, but a worn sensor has to be replaced. Standard repair: we replace the worn stick module with a new one. Hall Effect upgrade: we fit a stick that measures position with magnets instead of a rubbing contact. Nothing physically wears against the track, so it doesn't drift the same way again. No. The Mid 2014 and all Late 2015 21.5-inch models have RAM permanently soldered to the logic board. No upgrade is possible — not even with display removal. Only the Late 2013 21.5-inch has SO-DIMM slots that a technician can access. Can my 2013, 2014, or 2015 iMac 21.5-inch run macOS Sonoma? Yes, all three years can run Sonoma via OpenCore Legacy Patcher . The Late 2013 and Mid 2014 natively maxed out at Big Sur; Late 2015 at Monterey. iAssist performs the full OCLP upgrade for R1,500 — SSD and 8GB RAM required. My 2013 21.5-inch iMac has cracked glass — can just the glass be replaced? Yes. The Late 2013 21.5-inch iMac has a separate glass panel held by magnets in front of a separate LCD. Is an SSD upgrade worth it on these older models? Absolutely. These machines were shipped with slow spinning hard drives that are now years old. An SSD upgrade brings boot times from 4–5 minutes to under 20 seconds and transforms the overall experience. Combined with OCLP for Sonoma, the machine feels significantly faster. My 2013 or 2014 21.5-inch iMac makes a loud clicking noise from the hard drive — what does that mean? Clicking from a hard drive is a mechanical warning sign — the drive heads are failing to read correctly. This is a precursor to total drive failure and data loss. Stop using the machine for anything important, back up immediately if you can, and bring it in urgently. We can attempt data recovery from a clicking drive, but the window of opportunity closes fast. An SSD replacement after recovery prevents this from ever happening again. Can I still get replacement parts for a 2013 or 2015 21.5-inch iMac? The 2015 model is slightly less common but still serviceable. iAssist confirms parts availability during the free diagnostic before issuing any quote. R500 File system & storage architecture Recovery across HFS+, APFS, Fusion Drives & Apple Silicon Storage formats we recover from HFS+ (Mac OS Extended): Used on older spinning hard drives and HDDs in iMacs up to approximately 2017. Well-understood format with mature recovery tooling. High recovery rates for most failure modes. APFS (Apple File System): Used on SSDs from macOS High Sierra onwards. Copy-on-write architecture means recently deleted files often remain recoverable. Snapshot-based recovery also possible if Time Machine snapshots exist. Fusion Drive (CoreStorage logical volume group): A Fusion Drive presents as one volume but is actually a SATA HDD and a PCIe SSD managed by macOS CoreStorage. Recovery requires reassembling the logical volume group from both physical drives — one failing component can make the entire volume inaccessible. We recover from both drives independently and reconstruct where possible. FileVault encrypted volumes: If FileVault is enabled, the recovery password or iCloud recovery key is required. Without it, the volume cannot be decrypted and data is unrecoverable regardless of drive health. We advise clients to locate this before bringing the machine in. T2 chip & Apple Silicon — data recovery via board restoration T2 chip (2020 iMac): The T2 security chip encrypts all storage with keys tied to the specific T2 chip. If the T2 chip fails or the logic board is replaced, the storage encryption keys are lost and data cannot be recovered through any means — including chip desoldering. Recovery in T2 machines requires restoring the original logic board to working condition. Apple Silicon M1 / M3 / M4: Storage is integrated directly into the Apple Silicon package — it cannot be desoldered and read independently. Data recovery on these machines is only possible by restoring the logic board itself to a bootable state and then cloning the data normally. Non-T2 Intel iMac (2013–2019): The SSD blade or SATA drive can be connected directly to external recovery equipment. This is the most straightforward recovery path and has the highest success rate. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Common questions iMac fan and thermal service — FAQ Why is my iMac fan running at full speed all the time? Persistent maximum fan speed on an iMac is most commonly caused by dried-out thermal paste on the CPU and GPU, a failed temperature sensor IC, or a heavily dust-blocked heatsink and fan assembly. After years of operation the thermal compound dries and cracks, losing its ability to transfer heat efficiently — the iMac compensates by running the fan at full speed continuously. My iMac is getting very hot and running slowly — what is wrong? This is thermal throttling — when the CPU or GPU temperature exceeds a safe threshold, macOS reduces processor speed to limit heat output. The result is a machine that feels dramatically slower than it should be. Replacing the thermal paste and cleaning the internal dust brings temperatures down and full performance is restored immediately. How much does iMac fan and thermal service cost? The full thermal service is R2,500 — this covers display removal, CPU and GPU thermal compound replacement, full internal dust clean, and display reseal with OEM adhesive strips. It typically takes 2–3 hours depending on the iMac model and the scope of work required. Fan replacement if the fan bearing has failed is quoted separately after diagnostic. All pricing is confirmed in writing before work begins. How often should thermal paste be replaced on an iMac? On a heavily used iMac, thermal paste typically degrades significantly after 4 to 6 years. If your iMac is 5 years or older and running hot or loud, thermal paste replacement is almost certainly overdue. It is one of the most cost-effective ways to extend the life of an older machine. Can a dusty iMac cause permanent damage? Yes — prolonged high-temperature operation caused by dust blockage and degraded thermal paste accelerates wear on capacitors, GPU solder joints, and the logic board. AMD Radeon GPU failures on 27-inch iMacs are frequently accelerated by years of thermal stress. A thermal service is preventive maintenance as much as it is a repair. My iMac fan makes a grinding or rattling noise — is that fixable? Yes. A grinding or rattling fan has a failing bearing and should be replaced before it stops entirely. A seized fan causes the iMac to thermal throttle or shut down entirely to protect the processor. Fan replacement is straightforward and we carry fans for most iMac models. Will you clean the inside of my iMac while you have it open? Yes — a full internal dust clean is included in every thermal service. We clean the heatsink fins, fan blades, and all internal air channels while the display is open. If the iMac is opened for any other repair we also include the dust clean at no extra charge. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Common questions iMac liquid damage — FAQ My iMac got wet — what should I do right now? Do not attempt to power it on. This is the most important step. Powering on a wet iMac causes short-circuit damage that turns a recoverable situation into a much more expensive one. Disconnect the power cable immediately, leave the machine off, and bring it in to us as soon as possible. The sooner we get it into ultrasonic cleaning the better the recovery outcome. How does liquid get inside an iMac? The iMac draws cooling air in through ventilation slots at the bottom of the display. Drinks spilled nearby, office ceiling leaks, cleaning products sprayed near the machine, and air conditioning condensation all find their way in through these slots. Coffee and sugary drinks cause the most damage due to their corrosive residue. How much does iMac liquid damage repair cost? iMac liquid damage repair ranges from R900 to R2,800 depending on the extent of corrosion and the components affected. The power supply, logic board, and storage drive can all be affected. A free diagnostic determines which components sustained damage and the full repair scope is quoted in writing before work begins. Can you recover data from a liquid-damaged iMac? In many cases yes — particularly if the storage drive itself was not the primary impact point. We assess the drive during the diagnostic and advise on data recovery options. We always attempt data preservation before any further work begins if data recovery is requested. What is ultrasonic cleaning and why is it needed? Ultrasonic cleaning uses high-frequency sound waves in a specialist cleaning solution to remove corrosion, mineral deposits, and residue from the logic board at a microscopic level. It is far more effective than manual cleaning for liquid-damaged boards and is essential for complete corrosion removal. Without it, residue left on the board causes progressive corrosion that eventually causes secondary failures weeks or months after the initial incident. My iMac was damaged by liquid weeks ago — is it too late to repair? It is not too late, but time matters. Corrosion progresses continuously on an untreated board. A board that was wet a week ago has more corrosion than one wet yesterday. We have successfully recovered iMacs that sat wet for extended periods — but the sooner you bring it in the better the outcome and the lower the repair cost. Will everything work after liquid damage repair? In most cases yes — when liquid damage is treated promptly and the corrosion has not spread to critical components. In some cases individual ICs or the power supply may need replacement. We give you a full assessment after the ultrasonic clean and confirm exactly what is and isn't recoverable before any further work. Do you offer collection for liquid-damaged iMacs? Yes — R500 door-to-door collection across Gauteng. Keep the iMac powered off and disconnected until our courier arrives. This level of specificity is why we can fix machines that Apple and most repair centres write off as unrepairable. Common power rail & IC failures we service under the microscope PPBUS_G3H short: The main power bus shorted to ground — common after load-shedding surges. Identified via resistance measurement; faulty MOSFET or capacitor located and replaced. ISL6259 / ISL9221 charging IC: Controls power delivery from the PSU to the logic board. Failure causes no-power or intermittent power symptoms. Chip replaced at component level. MOSFET failure on power rail: MOSFETs on the 12V, 5V, and 3.3V rails fail after thermal stress or surge damage. Each rail tested individually; faulty FETs replaced. EFI / SPI ROM chip corruption: The boot firmware chip can corrupt after failed macOS updates or bad NVRAM writes. We reflash the ROM directly — machine boots again without board replacement. GPU die solder failure (AMD Radeon): Logic board replacement on affected 27-inch models. The machine returns to full normal operation post-replacement. SMC / T2 chip fault: System Management Controller faults cause fan-at-full, no-power, or display failures. Chip-level diagnosis performed before any replacement decision. iMac diagnostic LED guide — what each LED means LED 1 lit (only): Power from the wall is reaching the logic board. PSU is delivering standby voltage. Board-level fault or no power-on signal. LEDs 1 & 2 lit: Logic board is receiving power and the CPU has started. No GPU communication yet — GPU or VRAM fault likely. LEDs 1, 2 & 3 lit: GPU is communicating with the display. If screen is dark, fault is in the display panel, backlight, or cable — not the board. All 4 LEDs lit: Full system communication confirmed. If iMac still doesn't boot, fault is software or SSD — not hardware. No LEDs: No standby power reaching the board. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Common questions iMac macOS upgrade — FAQ What is OpenCore Legacy Patcher? OpenCore Legacy Patcher (OCLP) is an open-source project that allows older Mac models — dropped from official macOS support — to run the latest versions of macOS. It installs a custom bootloader that injects the necessary drivers and patches at startup, making it possible to run Sonoma or Ventura on 2013–2019 iMacs that Apple would otherwise restrict to Big Sur, Monterey, or Ventura. Which iMac models can be upgraded? iAssist supports OCLP upgrades on all iMac models from Late 2013 through 2019. This covers 21.5-inch and 27-inch Intel models across 2013, 2014, 2015, and 2017. 2019 iMacs run Sonoma natively and can be upgraded to Sequoia via OCLP. All models require an SSD and a minimum of 8GB RAM before the upgrade is performed. Why do I need an SSD? macOS Sonoma and Ventura are far more demanding on storage than older versions. Installing Sonoma onto a spinning hard drive or Fusion Drive results in an unusable experience — boot times of 5+ minutes and constant beachballing. An SSD brings boot times to under 20 seconds and makes the whole system feel fast. If your iMac still has a hard drive, we install an SSD first from R850 and then perform the OCLP upgrade. Why must my data be wiped? OCLP requires a clean macOS installation to work correctly. In-place upgrades from an older macOS using OpenCore frequently result in boot failures, broken drivers, and system instability. A clean wipe and fresh install is the only reliable method. Please back up everything important before dropping your iMac off — or ask us about our separate data migration service. Can you back up or restore my data? Data backup and post-install migration is available as a separate service, not included in the R1,500 OCLP fee. If you would like us to transfer your files and apps back onto the machine after the clean install, let us know when you book and we will quote you separately. We always recommend clients back up independently before any work begins. Will everything work after the upgrade? The vast majority of everyday functionality works normally after an OCLP installation — Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, iCloud, productivity apps, web browsers, and most creative software. Some GPU-accelerated effects on 2013–2014 machines may require root patching, which we apply as part of the service. We will advise you on any specific limitations for your model before work begins. Drop your iMac off in the morning and collect it the same afternoon or the following morning. Is it worth upgrading my old iMac rather than buying new? For most 2013–2019 iMacs in good working condition, the upgrade makes clear financial sense. A new iMac M4 starts at significantly more than the combined cost of an SSD upgrade and the OCLP service. After the upgrade your machine runs a current operating system, stays compatible with modern apps, and receives OCLP security patches for several more years. R500 Technical fault detail PSU internal failure modes & SMC diagnostics LiteOn & Delta PSU — common internal failure patterns Primary capacitor failure: The large electrolytic capacitors on the primary side of the PSU (typically 400V, 100–220µF) fail after years of thermal cycling and load-shedding stress. Symptoms: iMac dead or intermittent. These are replaceable at component level. Shorted bridge rectifier: The bridge rectifier converts AC from the wall to DC. Load-shedding surges can blow the rectifier instantly. Identified via continuity testing; replaced without full PSU swap in most cases. Secondary rail capacitor bulging: Lower-voltage output capacitors (5V, 12V rails) bulge and leak after extended high-temperature operation. Visible inspection confirms; replaced with equivalent-spec capacitors. Logic board safe-mode cutoff: The logic board monitors PSU output voltages and cuts power if rails deviate more than ±5%. A PSU delivering 11.4V on the 12V rail causes the board to shut down protectively — appearing as a dead iMac even though the logic board is healthy. Blown primary fuse: A surge can blow the glass fuse on the PSU primary input. A simple and inexpensive fix — but must be investigated to confirm the fuse didn't blow due to a downstream short on the logic board. Try an SMC reset before assuming the worst The System Management Controller (SMC) manages power, fans, and startup on Intel iMacs. A hung SMC can prevent startup even when all hardware is healthy. Intel iMac SMC reset: Shut down → unplug power cable → wait 15 seconds → plug back in → wait 5 seconds → press power button. This resets the SMC without losing any data. If the iMac starts after an SMC reset, the hardware is fine and the fault was an SMC state corruption — common after power interruptions. If the iMac remains completely unresponsive after an SMC reset with a known-good power outlet, the fault is hardware — bring it in for a free diagnostic. Apple Silicon (M1/M3/M4): There is no SMC — power management is handled by the secure enclave. Simply hold the power button for 10 seconds to force a shutdown, then restart normally. A completely dead iMac is most commonly caused by a failed power supply unit, a blown capacitor on the logic board power rail, or surge damage from load-shedding. Our technicians run a full board-level diagnostic to isolate whether the fault is in the PSU itself or on the logic board power circuit before quoting any repair. Can load-shedding damage an iMac power supply? Yes — and this is one of the most common iMac faults we see in South Africa. Power surges when Eskom restores supply, as well as the cumulative effect of repeated on-off cycles, can damage power supply capacitors and board-level power ICs. A surge protector or UPS significantly reduces this risk. If your iMac died around a load-shedding event, a power supply fault is the most likely cause. How much does iMac power supply repair cost? Intermittent power faults — where the iMac powers on some days but not others — usually point to a capacitor or transistor failing under temperature cycling. T1 chip — what you need to know How the T1 chip affects iMac Pro repairs Storage is encrypted by the T1 chip. Unlike pre-T1 Macs, you cannot simply remove the SSD and read it on another machine. The encryption keys are tied to the T1 chip on the original logic board. Data recovery requires the original board. If your iMac Pro logic board has failed, data recovery means restoring the board to a working state first — then cloning the data. We always attempt board restoration before declaring data unrecoverable. Logic board replacement = potential data loss. If the original board cannot be restored and must be replaced, the encrypted data on the SSD will not be accessible on the new board. Back up your iMac Pro regularly. Secure boot is enforced. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Common questions iMac Pro repair — FAQ Can the iMac Pro be repaired? Yes — but parts availability is the primary constraint. The iMac Pro was discontinued in 2021 and components are significantly rarer than those for the regular iMac line. iAssist performs a free diagnostic, identifies the exact fault, confirms parts availability, and gives you a written quote before any work begins. We will always be honest about what is and is not achievable. Can the RAM be upgraded on the iMac Pro? Technically yes — the iMac Pro uses ECC DDR4 2666MHz SO-DIMMs which are replaceable by a specialist. However, unlike the regular 27-inch iMac's rear panel, the iMac Pro requires full display removal and logic board extraction to access the RAM slots. Parts availability and cost are confirmed before quoting. What is the T1 chip and how does it affect repairs? The iMac Pro was the first Mac with a T1 security chip, which encrypts all storage and ties the encryption keys to that specific board. If the logic board fails, data cannot be recovered by simply removing the SSD — the original board must be restored to a working state first. iAssist always attempts board restoration before declaring data unrecoverable. My iMac Pro has Vega GPU artefacts — is it repairable? The AMD Radeon Pro Vega GPU is integrated into the logic board. GPU failure means logic board replacement. Parts are rare and expensive, and may require international sourcing. We give you a full written quote including parts cost and sourcing timeline — and if the repair cost is not economically sensible, we will tell you so. Do you offer collection for the iMac Pro? Yes — R500 insured door-to-door collection and return across Gauteng via Eliz Courier. The iMac Pro is heavy and we handle transport with care. WhatsApp us on 078 742 4769 to arrange. My iMac Pro shows No Bluetooth after a repair elsewhere — is that fixable? Yes — the iMac Pro Bluetooth module is connected via an internal cable that is easily dislodged during repair work. If Bluetooth disappeared after your machine was previously opened by another shop, it is almost certainly a disconnected or damaged antenna cable rather than a hardware failure. We see this regularly on machines that have been through inexperienced repair attempts. Free diagnostic to confirm — straightforward fix if it is the cable. Can the iMac Pro be upgraded to a faster processor? No. The Intel Xeon W processor in the iMac Pro is soldered directly to the logic board in a BGA package — it cannot be removed or upgraded. The iMac Pro's performance tier is fixed at the configuration purchased. RAM can be upgraded with specialist sourcing and full disassembly, but the CPU and GPU are permanently integrated into the board. R500 Signs you need more RAM Is your iMac starved for memory? Spinning beachball constantly The most common sign of RAM pressure. macOS is waiting for memory to free up before responding. Apps slow down with multiple windows Each app needs RAM to stay active. When RAM runs out macOS starts swapping to the SSD — much slower. Memory Pressure shows yellow or red Open Activity Monitor → Memory tab. Yellow or red pressure means your system is struggling. Swap Used is above zero Any Swap Used value means your Mac is using the SSD as overflow RAM. A RAM upgrade eliminates this. Parallels / Windows VM runs poorly Virtual machines need dedicated RAM to run smoothly. 8GB shared between macOS and Windows is not enough. Browser with 10+ tabs causes slowdowns Modern browsers are memory-hungry. 32+ tabs on 8GB causes constant reloading and beachballing. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Common questions iMac RAM upgrade — FAQ How much does an iMac RAM upgrade cost? iAssist charges R1,600 per 8GB DDR4 module. A 27-inch iMac upgrade from 8GB to 32GB uses four 8GB sticks at R6,400, or you can add just two sticks to bring an existing 8GB machine to 24GB. We will confirm the optimal configuration for your specific model before ordering. Which iMac models support a RAM upgrade? The iMac 27-inch from 2013 through 2020 (Intel) has user-accessible RAM via a panel on the rear — no display removal required and upgrades are available up to 64GB (2013–2014 DDR3) or 128GB (2015–2020 DDR4). The iMac 21.5-inch from 2013–2015 can be upgraded but requires full display removal. The iMac 21.5-inch from 2017 onwards and all Apple Silicon iMacs (M1, M3, M4) have RAM integrated into the chip — no upgrade is possible. Does the iMac 27-inch RAM upgrade require opening the display? No — the 27-inch Intel iMac has a dedicated RAM access panel on the rear of the machine that opens in seconds with no tools. Sticks slide in, panel closes. No display removal, no adhesive, no risk to the screen. Most 27-inch upgrades are complete in under an hour. How much RAM does my iMac actually need? For general use, web browsing, and email 8GB is workable but 16GB makes a noticeable difference. For Lightroom, Final Cut Pro, Parallels, or keeping 20+ browser tabs open, 32GB is the sweet spot. If you use virtual machines or heavy video work, 64GB or more makes sense on the 27-inch models. How do I know if I need more RAM? Open Activity Monitor, click the Memory tab, and look at Memory Pressure at the bottom. Yellow or red pressure means your Mac is struggling. Also check Swap Used — if this is anything other than zero your Mac is using the much slower SSD as overflow memory and more RAM will make an immediate difference. Can I add RAM to my existing sticks or must I replace all of them? On the 27-inch iMac you can add matched pairs to empty slots without replacing existing sticks, provided the new modules match the speed of the existing ones. We check your current configuration before ordering to ensure compatibility and optimal performance. How long does an iMac RAM upgrade take? 27-inch iMac RAM upgrades are completed same day — often within an hour if you drop off in the morning. 21.5-inch upgrades that require display removal take 3 to 4 hours due to the additional work involved. All pricing is confirmed after a free diagnostic — you receive a written fixed-price quote before any work begins. What is the difference between the glass and the LCD panel? iMac models from 2013 to 2014 have a separate front glass held by magnets and a separate LCD behind it. If only the glass is cracked with no visible image damage, only the glass needs replacing. From 2015 onwards Apple fused the glass directly to the LCD — they are one laminated unit and must be replaced together, which increases the cost. My iMac screen is black but it still runs — is that the display or the logic board? Connect an external monitor via Thunderbolt or HDMI. The display is carefully lifted, the damaged component replaced, and the display resealed with fresh OEM-grade adhesive strips. We also perform a full internal dust clean while the display is open. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Common questions iMac SSD upgrade — FAQ How much does an iMac SSD upgrade cost? iAssist charges R3,800 for a 500GB SSD upgrade where we supply the drive. This includes the SSD (R1,600), OEM adhesive strips (R400), full labour for display removal, internal dust clean, and reseal. If you supply your own compatible SSD, the fitting cost is R1,800 which includes adhesive strips and the same full service. Why does an iMac SSD upgrade cost more than a MacBook upgrade? Unlike a MacBook, opening an iMac requires carefully removing the entire display using professional separation tools and a controlled heating process. The display is sealed with adhesive strips which must be replaced on reseal. This adds significant labour compared to a MacBook where the base simply unscrews. We also perform a full internal dust clean while the display is open. What is a Fusion Drive and is it worth replacing? A Fusion Drive combines a small SSD with a spinning hard drive managed by macOS to appear as one volume. As the spinning drive ages it becomes the bottleneck and the iMac slows significantly. Replacing the entire Fusion Drive with a single pure SSD eliminates this bottleneck completely and is one of the most impactful upgrades you can make on an older iMac. Will my data be migrated to the new SSD? Data migration is included in the SSD upgrade service. We clone your existing drive to the new SSD so your files, apps, and settings transfer exactly. All Intel iMac models from 2013 onwards can have their internal storage replaced with an SSD. The 27-inch models from 2017–2020 also have a PCIe NVMe blade slot accessible without opening the display for an additional SSD. iMac M1, M3, and M4 models have storage integrated into the chip and cannot be upgraded. How long does an iMac SSD upgrade take? Most iMac SSD upgrades are completed within 4 to 6 hours. We call you when ready. Drop off in the morning and collect same afternoon in most cases. My iMac 27-inch already has a small SSD blade — can I upgrade it? Yes. The 27-inch iMac from 2017–2020 has a PCIe NVMe blade slot that can be upgraded to a larger, faster drive without removing the display. This is a quick same-day job. Try connecting to power for 30 minutes before pressing the power button. If it still won't respond, the battery may need replacement. https://iassist.net.za/pages/ipad-button.text: id="MainContent" class="content-for-layout focus-none" role="main" tabindex="-1"> iPad Button Repair Johannesburg | iAssist Home → iPad Repairs → Button Repair Free diagnostic · Home button · Power button · Volume · Side Touch ID · 6-month warranty iPad Button Repair Johannesburg & Gauteng Buttons take more abuse than they get credit for — the power button mashed through a boring Teams call, the volume rocker worn smooth by a toddler’s favourite show on repeat, the Home button clicked into early retirement by a fidgety commute. iAssist repairs Home buttons, power buttons, volume buttons, and side Touch ID buttons on all iPad models. Honest advice on Touch ID pairing before any Home button replacement. Free diagnostic. 6-month warranty. Button-related repairs on iPad fall into two very different categories depending on the generation: Home-button models (most pre-2020 iPads) use a mechanical Touch ID button that can fail from wear or drop damage, while Home-button-free models moved Touch ID into the top or side power button — a smaller, more drop-exposed sensor that fails more often from impact than from age. Neither Touch ID location can simply be swapped between units; each sensor is factory-paired to its own logic board. Note: Touch ID will not function on a replacement Home button without Apple's pairing process — we advise on this before repair. Power button stuck or won't click Physical damage or mechanism failure. Power button replacement restores normal sleep/wake and shutdown functionality. Volume buttons not responding Volume buttons share a flex cable. One or both sides not responding indicates flex cable or button mechanism failure. Side button Touch ID not working — Air 4+ / Mini 6+ iPads without a Home button have Touch ID in the side power button. A failed side button affects both power control and fingerprint authentication. Home button feels mushy or stuck Debris under the button or a degraded button mechanism. Cleaning and mechanism replacement. https://iassist.net.za/pages/ipad-chargi.text: id="MainContent" class="content-for-layout focus-none" role="main" tabindex="-1"> iPad Charging Port Repair Johannesburg | iAssist Home → iPad Repairs → Charging Port Repair Free diagnostic · Modular port swap R2,500 · Micro-soldering · Charging IC · Lightning & USB-C iPad Charging Port Repair Johannesburg & Gauteng More "my iPad won't charge" visits than you'd think turn out to be nothing more than a pocket's worth of lint packed into the port — the tech equivalent of a blocked stormwater drain after the first proper Highveld thunderstorm. iAssist repairs iPad Lightning and USB-C charging ports across all models. iPad Pro and Air 7 have modular ports — swappable for R2,500. Standard iPad and older Air models use soldered ports repaired with precision micro-soldering. Charging IC faults also repaired at component level. Whether a charging port repair is a same-day job or a longer micro-soldering job depends entirely on the port design Apple used for that specific model: the Thunderbolt/USB-C port on M1-generation iPad Pro onward, and the M3-generation Air, is modular and swaps as a single part in a few hours, while the soldered USB-C ports used on standard iPads, most Air models, and pre-M1 Pro units require the port to be desoldered and replaced under a microscope. Free diagnostic · Modular port swap R2,500 · Micro-soldering · Charging IC · Lightning & USB-C 📱 WhatsApp for a quote Call 078 742 4769 Free Diagnostic 4.9★ Google rating 6-month Warranty Written Quote first R300 Collection Charging faults we fix iPad charging port issues we see every day iPad not charging at all If the iPad shows no charging symbol with a known-good cable and charger, the fault is likely a damaged port, compacted lint, a faulty charging IC, or a dead battery. Free diagnostic confirms the exact cause before any work begins. Charging IC fault — charges but battery won't increase A charging symbol with no battery increase (or very slow increase) indicates the charging IC on the logic board has failed. The port is making contact but the power management circuit is not routing charge to the battery. Micro-soldering repair to replace the charging IC — this is a common fault on all iPad models. Loose or damaged Lightning / USB-C port Physical damage, a bent or broken pin inside the port, or a cracked port socket prevents reliable charging. Soldered ports on standard iPad and Air 1–6 require micro-soldering. Modular ports on iPad Pro and Air 7 can be swapped directly. Compacted lint blocking the port Lint from pockets and bags compacts into Lightning and USB-C ports over time, preventing the cable from seating fully. We clean ports as part of the free diagnostic — often this alone restores charging without needing a repair. iPad charges only in certain positions If the iPad only charges when the cable is held at a specific angle, a pin inside the port is bent or partially broken. Micro-soldering to repair or replace the port. Water-damaged charging port Corrosion inside the port from liquid exposure prevents charging contact. Ultrasonic cleaning and port replacement where required. Charging port repair pricing iPad charging port repair — iAssist prices iPad Pro (all generations) and iPad Air 7 (M3) have a modular USB-C port — direct swap, no soldering required. All other iPads have a soldered port — micro-soldering repair required. Charging IC fault (no charge despite good port) priced separately after diagnostic — typically R1,500–R2,000. https://iassist.net.za/pages/ipad-data-r.meta: iPad data recovery Johannesburg. Dead iPads, liquid damage, boot loop, broken screen. No data no charge. Free diagnostic. WhatsApp 078 742 4769.
https://iassist.net.za/pages/ipad-data-r.text: id="MainContent" class="content-for-layout focus-none" role="main" tabindex="-1"> iPad Data Recovery Johannesburg | iAssist Home → iPad Repairs → Data Recovery No data no charge · Board-level recovery · Liquid damage · Boot loop · Broken screen iPad Data Recovery Johannesburg & Gauteng Backing up to iCloud is a bit like buying insurance — everyone means to get around to it, usually right after the day they actually needed it. iAssist recovers data from dead, liquid-damaged, boot-looping, and broken-screen iPads. All M-series and modern iPads use hardware encryption — data recovery requires the original board to be functional. No data, no charge. Free diagnostic. Recovering data from a dead or liquid-damaged iPad is more involved than on iPhone, because iPad storage is soldered NAND with no independent power path once the board itself is compromised — our process is to stabilise the board first, then attempt a data clone before any other repair work begins, so a logic board repair never risks the data already on the device. If we can't recover anything, there's no charge for the attempt. No data no charge · Board-level recovery · Liquid damage · Boot loop · Broken screen 📱 WhatsApp for a quote Call 078 742 4769 Free Diagnostic 4.9★ Google rating 6-month Warranty Written Quote first R300 Collection Data recovery situations we handle Common iPad data recovery scenarios iPad completely dead — data still needed If the logic board can be repaired, all data is preserved. We attempt board repair first before declaring data unrecoverable. The encryption model on all modern iPads means data cannot be extracted without the original board being functional. Liquid damaged iPad — photos and files needed Liquid damage recovery prioritises board functionality first. Once the board is repaired and the iPad powers on, all data is accessible. Success rate is significantly higher when the device is brought in quickly after the incident. Screen shattered — iPad still powers on If the iPad powers on but the screen is too damaged to use, we can replace the screen to gain full access to your data. This is the simplest and fastest data recovery scenario. Boot loop or stuck on Apple logo Repeated Apple logo or boot loops are often software-recoverable without data loss. https://iassist.net.za/pages/ipad-liquid.text: id="MainContent" class="content-for-layout focus-none" role="main" tabindex="-1"> iPad Liquid Damage Repair Johannesburg | iAssist Home → iPad Repairs → Liquid Damage Do not charge a wet iPad · Ultrasonic cleaning · Component-level recovery · Free diagnostic iPad Liquid Damage Repair Johannesburg & Gauteng Every family WhatsApp group has an uncle ready with rice-bag advice — ignore him and get it to us instead. iAssist treats liquid-damaged iPads with professional ultrasonic cleaning and component-level board repair. Do not charge or turn on a wet iPad — bring it in immediately. The sooner we see it, the better the recovery rate. Free diagnostic. The single biggest factor in whether a liquid-damaged iPad survives is how quickly it's brought in before the corrosion progresses — power should stay off and charging should never be attempted once a spill is suspected, since applying power across a shorted or corroding trace is what turns a recoverable fault into board-level damage. Our process starts with ultrasonic cleaning to remove residue and corrosion, followed by board-level testing to isolate any component that failed as a result of the exposure. Do not charge a wet iPad · Ultrasonic cleaning · Component-level recovery · Free diagnostic 📱 WhatsApp for a quote Call 078 742 4769 Free Diagnostic 4.9★ Google rating 6-month Warranty Written Quote first R300 Collection Liquid damage faults we treat Water damage situations we see every day iPad exposed to water — act immediately Do not turn on, charge, or dry with heat. Turn off immediately if still on. Bring in within 24 hours for the best recovery rate. Every hour of delay allows corrosion to spread further across the board. iPad was in salt water or pool Salt water and pool chemicals are significantly more corrosive than fresh water. Same urgent procedure — turn off, do not charge, bring in immediately. Recovery is possible but requires faster action. iPad works after water but acting strange An iPad that survived a water incident but is now glitching, dropping Wi-Fi, having touch issues, or running hot has internal corrosion spreading. Bring it in before a component fails completely. iPad won't charge after liquid damage Corrosion on the charging port or charging IC is the most common post-liquid-damage fault. Ultrasonic cleaning followed by port or IC repair where required. Screen issues after water exposure Liquid inside the display causes dark spots, bleed, or discolouration. If the LCD has been damaged by liquid, it needs replacement after the board is cleaned and confirmed working. iPad turned on after water damage and now dead Powering on a wet iPad is the most common way to cause permanent board damage — electricity and water cause immediate short circuits and burn out ICs. Recovery is still attempted but success rate is lower than for iPads that were not powered on after the incident. https://iassist.net.za/pages/ipad-logic-.text: id="MainContent" class="content-for-layout focus-none" role="main" tabindex="-1"> iPad Logic Board Repair Johannesburg | iAssist Home → iPad Repairs → Logic Board Repair Free diagnostic · No power · Charging IC · Micro-soldering · Face ID · Surge damage iPad Logic Board Repair Johannesburg & Gauteng Micro-soldering under a microscope takes steadier hands than parallel parking on Empire Road at rush hour — precision work, no room for a wobble. iAssist performs component-level micro-soldering repairs on iPad logic boards — no power, charging IC failures, backlight faults, Face ID issues, and surge damage. We repair faults other shops decline. Free diagnostic before any quote. A no-power or no-charge iPad is very rarely a dead board outright — it's far more often one failed component on the board, most commonly the charging IC or a short caused by liquid ingress. We diagnose at board level under a microscope before recommending any repair, which is why component-level micro-soldering typically costs a fraction of Apple's whole-unit replacement quote and, critically, doesn't touch the data already on the device. Free diagnostic · No power · Charging IC · Micro-soldering · Face ID · Surge damage 📱 WhatsApp for a quote Call 078 742 4769 Free Diagnostic 4.9★ Google rating 6-month Warranty Written Quote first R300 Collection Logic board faults we fix iPad board-level issues we see every day iPad won't turn on — no power The most common logic board fault. Usually caused by a failed charging IC, a dead power management IC, or corrosion from liquid damage. Free diagnostic to isolate the fault before any work begins. Charging IC failure The iPad shows a charging symbol or is connected to power but the battery never increases. The charging IC on the board has failed and is not routing power to the battery. Micro-soldering repair — component replaced at board level. No power after liquid damage Liquid damage corrodes the board and can kill the power path, charging circuit, or multiple ICs simultaneously. Ultrasonic cleaning followed by component-level diagnosis and repair of damaged chips. Face ID not working after repair If Face ID stopped working after a screen replacement, the issue is likely a damaged or disconnected Face ID flex cable. If the Secure Enclave itself has failed, Face ID cannot be restored — honest assessment provided after diagnostic. iPad turns on but crashes or boot loops Repeated crashes, stuck on Apple logo, or boot loops can indicate storage failure, RAM faults, or an unstable power circuit. Diagnostic determines whether it is a software or hardware fault. Backlight failure — screen dark, image visible in light A faint image visible in direct light with no backlight indicates the backlight driver IC on the board has failed. Micro-soldering repair to replace the backlight IC. Surge or power damage Power surges from load shedding spikes or incorrect chargers can kill protection circuits on the logic board. Specific ICs are replaced at component level rather than replacing the entire board. We confirm exact pricing in writing after your free diagnostic, before any work starts. What's the difference between an iPad screen and digitiser? The "screen" combines two layers: the LCD (which displays the image) and the digitiser (the glass touch layer on top). On older iPads they are separate — meaning a cracked digitiser with working LCD is a cheaper repair. On all newer iPads (iPad Air 4 onwards, all iPad Pro from 2018, all current iPads) the layers are bonded together — meaning the entire assembly must be replaced. Your free diagnostic confirms which type you have. Can you repair an iPad Pro M4? Yes. We repair all current iPad Pro M-series models including M4. The M4 iPad Pro uses an OLED display assembly which is more expensive to replace than older LCD-based models, but battery, charging port, speakers, and most logic board faults are repairable at component level. Free diagnostic gives you the exact cost upfront. My iPad won't charge. What could it be? Three common causes: a damaged charging port (Lightning pins worn or USB-C bent), a failed charging IC on the logic board, or a degraded battery that won't accept charge. We diagnose this for free — port repair is typically same-day, charging IC replacement takes 1–2 days, battery replacement is same-day on most models. My iPad has random touches happening on its own. What's wrong? This is "ghost touch" or touch IC failure — most common on iPad 5/6/7, iPad Mini 5, and older iPad Air models. The touch controller chip on the logic board has failed. A screen replacement won't fix it — only chip-level board repair will. We perform this repair under microscope with full warranty. How long does iPad repair take? Screen and battery replacements are typically same-day or next-day. Charging port and speaker repairs are usually same-day. Liquid damage treatment is 2–3 business days depending on severity. Logic board chip-level repairs (touch IC, charging IC) take 1–3 business days. We confirm timing at the time of your free diagnostic. My iPad got wet — what should I do? Power off immediately if it's still on. Do not turn it on, charge it, or try to dry it with a hairdryer or rice. Bring it to us within 48 hours for the best recovery outcome — corrosion develops the longer liquid sits on the board. We use ultrasonic cleaning at component level. iPad liquid damage recovery rate sits around 85% when the device arrives within 24–48 hours. Is it worth fixing an older iPad? Almost always — for school iPads, kitchen recipe iPads, GPS in vehicles, or kids' devices, repair is far cheaper than replacement. A new entry-level iPad costs over R7,000. A screen replacement on an older iPad is R1,500 – R3,500 and gives you another 2–4 years. We'll tell you honestly during the free diagnostic if a repair isn't worth doing. If the same fault recurs within 6 months, we'll fix it at no charge. Our warranty applies to every repair type, from screen replacements to logic board work. Can you collect my iPad? Yes. ID & Touch ID Face ID repair — JCID tag-on / dot projector re-pairing R1,600 Face ID repair — IC on MLB Assessment + quote Known issues on the iPhone 11 Pro Max — read before booking ⚠ Battery degradation — critical at 6 years At six years old, the iPhone 11 series battery is the single most common repair we see on these devices. Six years of daily charge cycles leaves most batteries well below Apple's 80% service threshold — and many significantly below that. At this level of degradation, iOS performance throttling is active, the device feels noticeably slower, and battery life may be measured in hours rather than a full day. Check Settings → Battery → Battery Health. Below 80% is Apple's service recommendation. Below 70% — common on heavily used 6-year-old devices — the device may shut down unexpectedly at 20–30% charge, charge slowly, or generate significant heat during charging. Battery replacement on the iPhone 11 series is the single best-value repair available — restoring full performance, removing throttling, and extending daily life dramatically. Same-day replacement available at our Silvamonte centre. ⚠ OLED burn-in — common at 6 years on heavy-use devices The Super Retina XDR OLED panels on the iPhone 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max are showing burn-in on heavily used devices at this age. OLED burn-in occurs when the same image is displayed at high brightness for extended periods — the organic compounds in the OLED pixels degrade unevenly, leaving a permanent ghost image visible particularly on light or white backgrounds. Common burn-in patterns on iPhone 11 Pro: Ghost of the status bar (time, signal bars, battery icon) visible as a faint permanent overlay. Ghost of the keyboard visible at the bottom of the screen. Navigation bar ghosts on white backgrounds. Burn-in is permanent — it cannot be corrected by software or settings. Screen replacement with a new or used original OLED panel resolves it. We also offer OLED glass-only refurbishment if the panel is working but the glass is cracked without significant burn-in. ⚠ Hydra charging IC failure — Lightning charging fault at this age The iPhone 11 series uses the Hydra IC (the successor to the Tristar U2 chip used on earlier models) to manage all Lightning charging communication, USB authentication, and power delivery. After six years of daily use — particularly if cheap, non-MFi certified Lightning cables have been used — the Hydra IC fails at a significant rate on this generation. Symptoms of Hydra IC failure: "This accessory may not be supported" with Lightning cables that worked previously Won't charge at all — cable plugged in, nothing happens, no charging icon Won't charge on Lightning but charges wirelessly — this is 80% Hydra IC, 20% charging port Doesn't appear in iTunes / Finder when plugged into a computer Very slow charging — draws minimal current despite a working cable and adapter Overheating near the Lightning port during charging attempts Won't turn on at all — in severe Hydra failure, the phone cannot boot because the Hydra IC manages I2C data lines that the backlight driver and bootloader depend on Cause: Cheap, uncertified Lightning cables — particularly cables bought at petrol stations, market stalls, or bundled with non-Apple accessories — do not include the correct E75 authentication chip that Apple's Hydra IC expects. Without this handshake, the unfiltered current from the charger reaches the Hydra IC directly, causing progressive damage and eventual failure. A single power surge through a cheap cable can kill the IC immediately. This is a micro-soldering repair — the Hydra IC is removed under microscope and replaced. We perform this regularly on the iPhone 11 series. Free diagnostic before any work is quoted. ⚠ TrueDepth camera damage — very common on iPhone 11 series, specialist repair TrueDepth camera damage and Face ID failure is one of the most common iPhone 11 and 11 Pro repairs we see. The TrueDepth system comprises multiple components — dot projector, infrared (IR) camera, flood illuminator, and earpiece/sensor flex cable — and any one of them failing produces the same result: Face ID unavailable. How iAssist repairs TrueDepth camera faults — JCID tag on flex: We use the JCID tag method on the flex cable to repair TrueDepth camera faults on the iPhone 11 series. This specialist technique reads and writes the authentication data associated with the TrueDepth components, allowing the Face ID system to be restored after flex cable damage or component replacement — without the need for an original paired donor assembly. If the repair is viable, Face ID is fully restored to normal operation. When the JCID method cannot fix it — IR camera failure: If the infrared (IR) camera itself has failed, no flex repair or JCID tag method can restore Face ID. The IR camera on the iPhone 11 series is cryptographically paired to the device at the factory — it cannot be swapped from another phone or replaced with a new unit. If the IR camera is the fault, Face ID cannot be recovered on that device. We diagnose this specifically during our TrueDepth assessment and tell you clearly before charging anything. Price: R1,500 — if the fault is repairable via JCID flex tag, across all iPhone 11, 11 Pro, and 11 Pro Max models. If the IR camera is confirmed as the fault and Face ID cannot be recovered, there is no charge for the diagnostic. If your iPhone 11 lost Face ID after a screen replacement at another shop, or if it has gradually stopped working — bring it in for a free TrueDepth diagnostic. We assess, confirm whether it is repairable, and quote before any work begins. ⚠ No SIM / No Service — Transceiver IC fault iPhone 11 models are increasingly presenting with baseband and No SIM faults at this age. The most common board-level cause is failure of the Transceiver IC (XCVR_K — PMB5765) on the logic board. This chip manages cellular radio transmission and reception. When it fails, the iPhone shows "No SIM Installed" despite a working SIM, or loses all cellular service permanently. Additional causes include the inductor FL8442 at the bottom of the logic board — located near the upper antenna connector and very easily damaged during disassembly. If No SIM appeared immediately after a repair (screen replacement, battery replacement), FL8442 damage during that repair is the likely cause. Both are micro-soldering repairs. We diagnose the exact fault before quoting — free assessment, quote in writing before any work begins. ⚠ NAND storage failure — stuck in iTunes / DFU mode, P15 programmer repair iPhone 11 series devices are coming in regularly with NAND-related failures — and this is one of the most mishandled repairs in the industry. The NAND flash storage chip has a finite number of read and write cycles. At six years of daily use — particularly on devices that were heavily used for photos, apps, and frequent iOS updates — the NAND chip develops worn sectors, bad blocks, and degraded read/write speeds that cause the device to fail in ways that look like software problems but are not. What many shops get wrong: When an iPhone 11 is stuck in iTunes or DFU mode and restore keeps failing, the most common response at general repair shops is to repeatedly attempt DFU restores — sometimes charging for a "software repair" — without ever diagnosing the underlying hardware cause. A NAND failure cannot be resolved by any software restore. The restore fails because the NAND chip cannot complete the write process reliably. Attempting more restores does not fix this and wastes the customer's time and money. Common symptoms of NAND failure on the iPhone 11 series: Stuck in iTunes / recovery mode — device shows the USB cable and iTunes/Finder logo. Restore starts but fails with error codes 4013, 9, 14, or 21. Progress bar begins then the restore aborts. DFU restore loop — device enters DFU mode, restore begins, fails with the same error code every attempt. Extremely slow performance — the device is inexplicably sluggish even after a battery replacement. App launches take 30–60 seconds. iOS feels unresponsive. The NAND is failing to serve read requests at normal speed. Bootloop that software cannot fix — device restarts continuously; no amount of restoring resolves it. The repair — NAND replacement using the P15 programmer: We use the P15 NAND programmer to replace and correctly program the NAND chip on the iPhone 11 series. This specialist tool reads and writes the device's unique identifier data — serial number, Wi-Fi MAC address, and baseband information — from the original NAND and programs it into the replacement chip. Without correct programming via a tool like the P15, the replacement NAND will not allow the device to activate. This is the difference between a properly executed NAND replacement and a device that restores but cannot connect to Apple's servers. Storage upgrade to 256GB — recommended when replacing NAND: Since the board is already open and the NAND micro-soldering work is being performed, we strongly recommend upgrading the storage to 256GB at the same time. The NAND chip is the primary cost — upgrading the capacity adds minimal cost relative to the total repair while giving the device a fresh chip with maximum remaining write cycles and significantly more storage. Many iPhone 11 series devices came in 64GB or 128GB configurations where storage was already a limitation. If your iPhone 11 is stuck in iTunes or DFU mode and restore keeps failing — this is almost certainly a NAND issue, not a software problem. Bring it in for a free board-level diagnostic.
