My iPhone 15/16 won't charge past 1% — is that fixable, or should I write it off? It's fixable, and it's more common than people think — that symptom (stuck on 1%, won't charge, occasionally the touchscreen stops responding) is a failed U9500 charging IC on the logic board. Despite how many repair counters Fourways has, this is board-level work most of them don't do — it means desoldering and replacing the chip directly, then reflashing the EEPROM. We do this in-house, usually 24 to 72 hours, with a 6-month warranty attached. And if you'd rather not wait for a courier, you're only 20 minutes away. A kiosk at Fourways Mall or Montecasino already turned me away — is there any point trying you? Definitely a point. Fourways has more repair options than most areas, but nearly all of them are Level 2 — screens and batteries, nothing deeper. Charging IC failure, Face ID, logic board faults and liquid damage all get declined or quoted as a replacement. That's precisely the work we specialise in, so come to us before you write the phone off. Screen or battery job — should I just drop in, or is courier just as fast? Honestly, either works well from Fourways. Drop-in is quickest for screens and batteries: 20 minutes down William Nicol, 2–4 hours in the workshop, home the same day. If it's a board-level fault needing 1–3 days anyway, the courier is no slower — we collect, repair, and return it for a flat R300, and you never have to leave home. Either route starts with a free diagnostic and a written quote. Which suburbs around Fourways does the courier actually collect from? The full spread — Broadacres, Lonehill, Dainfern, Northriding, Olivedale, Paulshof, Magaliessig, Witkoppen and Beverley are all covered. R300 flat for the round trip, fully insured, and we photograph the device at both collection and return so there's a record. WhatsApp 078 742 4769 to book a slot. We just relocated to Fourways — does a recently-transferred or newly set-up iPhone need anything special before a repair? Not really, no — we get this a lot given how fast Fourways is growing; over 40,000 new homes are underway or planned across developments like Steyn City, Riversands and Chartwell, so plenty of the iPhones we see are only weeks into a new SIM, a new Apple ID transfer, or a first-phone setup for a child starting at a local school. A screen or battery repair doesn't touch any of your iCloud data, contacts, or app setup — the phone comes back exactly as it went in. The only thing we'd ask is that Find My iPhone is switched off, or that you know the Apple ID password, so we can test the repair without it locking against activation. Is there an Apple Store at Fourways Mall, or just a reseller? Just a reseller — South Africa has no Apple-owned retail stores anywhere in the country, only Apple Premium Resellers. iStore does have a store at Fourways Mall (Shop NG24), a legitimate option for buying new Apple products or an in-warranty repair on a very recent device. Board-level faults — charging IC failure, logic board damage, liquid damage past a surface wipe — aren't something Apple Premium Resellers generally handle in-house, though. That's specialist bench work, which is exactly what we do daily. Will an independent repair here void my Apple warranty, or put my data at risk? No on both counts, generally. Apple's 2017 policy update means a third-party screen or battery repair only voids Apple's cover on that specific repair, not your whole warranty — and further charges would only apply if the repair itself damaged another part of the phone. We use OEM-grade parts throughout and add our own 6-month warranty on every job. Your storage chip isn't touched during a screen, battery, or most board-level repairs, so photos and apps are unaffected — though we'd still suggest a quick backup beforehand, just as a precaution. booking ⚠ No touch and/or random 3-minute restart — board-level design defect, ~50% success rate The iPhone SE 2020 has a well-documented and specific board-level design defect that causes two related but distinct symptoms — either independently or together: No touch / intermittent touch — the touchscreen stops registering input completely, or works then randomly fails. Replacing the screen with a brand new display makes no difference — the fault is not in the screen. 3-minute restart loop — the iPhone restarts every 3 minutes on a precise timer. The panic log shows: "Missing sensor(s): mic1" — the mic1 sensor on the charging port flex cannot be detected by the CPU. Why both symptoms come from the same fault: Inside the logic board, three signal traces run through the PCB layers under the SIM tray area. These traces carry the mic1 sensor signal (needed by thermalmonitord every 3 minutes) and the touch digitiser signal (needed continuously). When these traces break inside the board — from drops, flex stress, or manufacturing weakness — both signals fail. The break is invisible from the outside. Step 1 — OEM charging port replacement first: mic1 lives on the charging port flex. We always test with a confirmed OEM pull charging port flex before touching the board. If the restart stops, no board work is needed. Cheap aftermarket flexes and iPhone 8 charging ports do not have the required thermal sensor — OEM pull parts only. Step 2 — Board-level jumper repair (if charging port doesn't fix it): When the break is inside the PCB, the fix requires running 3 long jumper wires inside the board to bypass the broken traces: 2 jumpers for mic1 — soldered to resistors on the side of the CPU, bypassing the broken I2C lines 1 jumper for touch — requires carefully scraping out the trace next to the SIM slot and running a wire to reconnect it We are honest about the success rate — approximately 50%. This is extremely precise micro-soldering work inside very confined traces on a compact board. The wires are long and run across the entire board. Even performed correctly, the repair does not always succeed due to the nature of trace damage inside a multi-layer PCB. We always discuss this with the customer before any board work begins, agree the approach and the risk clearly, and quote in writing. We do not charge for the diagnostic assessment — only for work you agree to proceed with knowing the odds. If your SE 2020 has no touch or reboots every 3 minutes — bring it in. Free diagnostic, OEM flex test first, honest conversation about the board repair before anything is committed. ⚠ Battery degradation — critical at 6 years At six years old, most SE 2020 batteries are well below Apple's 80% service threshold. The compact 4.7" body houses a smaller battery than larger iPhones — meaning each charge cycle is a larger proportion of total capacity, and degradation is felt more quickly than on larger models. By this age, performance throttling is active on most units and daily battery life is significantly shorter than when new. Check Settings → Battery → Battery Health. Below 80%, battery replacement is Apple's recommendation — and the single most impactful improvement available for the SE 2020. ⚠ Hydra charging IC — Lightning charging fault at this age The Hydra IC managing Lightning charging can fail on the SE 2020 at this age — particularly where cheap, uncertified Lightning cables have been used. Symptoms: won't charge on Lightning, "accessory not supported", charges on wireless but not cable. Charges wirelessly but not via Lightning? ~80% Hydra IC, ~20% Lightning port. Free diagnostic confirms which. Use Apple MFi-certified cables only. ✅ Component interchangeability — SE 2020, SE 2022, and iPhone 8 share most parts The iPhone SE 2020, SE 2022, and iPhone 8 are built around the same chassis design and share the majority of their hardware components. Apple essentially took the iPhone 8's body and upgraded the internals across each SE generation. Understanding this helps explain both why parts are widely available and where the differences lie. Interchangeable parts across SE 2020, SE 2022, and iPhone 8: Display / screen — fully interchangeable between SE 2020, SE 2022, and iPhone 8. Important: when swapping screens, the True Tone calibration data must be copied from the original display to the replacement — we transfer this data as part of every SE screen replacement to preserve accurate colour temperature. Frame / chassis — the aluminium frame is interchangeable across all three models. Colour swaps between SE 2020 and SE 2022 are straightforward. Charging port (Lightning) — the charging port flex is interchangeable. Note for SE 2020 restart repairs: only confirmed OEM pull charging ports should be used — the mic1 thermal sensor must be present on the flex. Rear camera — the 12MP single rear camera module is interchangeable across SE 2020, SE 2022, and iPhone 8. Other shared components — speakers, buttons, Taptic Engine, and antennas are all cross-compatible across the three models. The one key difference — batteries (not interchangeable): iPhone 8 battery: 1,821 mAh iPhone SE 2020 battery: 1,821 mAh — identical to the iPhone 8 iPhone SE 2022 battery: 2,018 mAh — larger capacity, unique to the SE 2022 The motherboard is also unique to each model — the SE 2020 uses an A13 chip, the SE 2022 uses an A15, and the iPhone 8 uses an A11. Every other major component is shared. This makes parts sourcing straightforward and repair costs competitive across all three models. ⚠ NAND storage failure — stuck in iTunes / DFU mode, P15 programmer repair The iPhone SE 2020 is now at an age where NAND flash storage wear is a regular repair we see. The NAND chip stores iOS, all apps, photos, and data — and after years of daily read and write operations, worn sectors and degraded write speeds cause failures that look like software problems but are not. What many shops get wrong: When a device is stuck in iTunes or DFU mode with restore failing, most shops attempt repeated DFU restores — sometimes charging for a "software repair" — without diagnosing the actual NAND hardware fault. A NAND failure cannot be resolved by any software restore. The restore fails because the NAND chip cannot complete the write process reliably. Symptoms: Stuck in iTunes / recovery mode with error codes 4013, 9, 14, or 21 during restore. DFU restore loop that always fails. Inexplicably slow performance even with a new battery. Bootloop that software cannot resolve. The repair: We use the P15 NAND programmer to replace and correctly program the NAND chip — including the device's unique serial number, Wi-Fi address, and baseband data. Without correct programming the device will not activate after NAND replacement. Upgrade to 256GB recommended: Since the board is open and the micro-soldering work is already being performed, we recommend upgrading to 256GB at the same time. Fresh chip, maximum write cycles remaining, significantly more storage — for minimal additional cost over the base NAND replacement. If your iPhone SE 2020 is stuck in iTunes or DFU mode and restore keeps failing — bring it in for a free board-level diagnostic before spending more time on software restores that will not work. If your SE 2022 won't charge via Lightning but charges wirelessly, that's ~80% Hydra IC and ~20% charging port. Free diagnostic confirms which before any work is quoted. The SE 2022 is the last SE model — keep it well maintained. ✅ Component interchangeability — SE 2020, SE 2022, and iPhone 8 share most parts The iPhone SE 2020, SE 2022, and iPhone 8 are built around the same chassis design and share the majority of their hardware components. Apple essentially took the iPhone 8's body and upgraded the internals across each SE generation. Understanding this helps explain both why parts are widely available and where the differences lie. Interchangeable parts across SE 2020, SE 2022, and iPhone 8: Display / screen — fully interchangeable between SE 2020, SE 2022, and iPhone 8. Frame / chassis — the aluminium frame is interchangeable across all three models. Colour swaps between SE 2020 and SE 2022 are straightforward. Charging port (Lightning) — the charging port flex is interchangeable. Note for SE 2020 restart repairs: only confirmed OEM pull charging ports should be used — the mic1 thermal sensor must be present on the flex. Rear camera — the 12MP single rear camera module is interchangeable across SE 2020, SE 2022, and iPhone 8. Other shared components — speakers, buttons, Taptic Engine, and antennas are all cross-compatible across the three models. The one key difference — batteries (not interchangeable): iPhone 8 battery: 1,821 mAh iPhone SE 2020 battery: 1,821 mAh — identical to the iPhone 8 iPhone SE 2022 battery: 2,018 mAh — larger capacity, unique to the SE 2022 The motherboard is also unique to each model — the SE 2020 uses an A13 chip, the SE 2022 uses an A15, and the iPhone 8 uses an A11. Every other major component is shared. This makes parts sourcing straightforward and repair costs competitive across all three models. ⚠ NAND storage failure — iTunes / DFU mode, P15 programmer repair NAND flash storage wear is increasingly appearing on iPhone SE 2022 devices — particularly heavily used units or those that have been close to full storage capacity for extended periods. The NAND chip has a finite number of read/write cycles, and when it begins to fail the device presents with symptoms that look like software problems. What many shops get wrong: Repeated DFU restores charged as "software repair" without diagnosing the hardware fault. A failing NAND cannot be fixed by any restore — the restore itself fails because the NAND cannot complete the write process. Error codes 4013, 9, 14, or 21 during restore, or DFU loops that never complete, point to NAND. The repair: NAND chip replaced using the P15 NAND programmer , which correctly programs the replacement chip with the device's unique identifiers. We recommend upgrading to 256GB when replacing NAND — the board is already open and the upgrade cost is minimal relative to the total repair. The SIM card is fine — the fault is in the iPhone's cellular hardware. Most likely: SIM tray contact damage, Transceiver IC failure (11 series — XCVR_K), or RF board solder joint failure (12 series). Free diagnostic under microscope determines which. What is the XCVR_K transceiver IC? The XCVR_K (PMB5765) is the cellular radio transceiver IC on the iPhone 11 series. It manages all cellular transmission and reception. After several years or drops, this chip fails and produces permanent No SIM. Board-level micro-soldering repair. My iPhone 11 shows No SIM after a battery replacement — what happened? The FL8442 inductor near the upper antenna connector on the 11 series is easily damaged during disassembly. If No SIM appeared immediately after a repair elsewhere, FL8442 damage during that repair is the most likely cause. My iPhone 12 Mini shows No SIM and no Wi-Fi after a drop — are those connected? Yes — the 12 Mini's compact board is susceptible to flex-induced solder joint failure. Drop impact cracks RF section connections, producing No SIM, No Service, and Wi-Fi failure simultaneously. A board reball typically resolves both. What is the difference between No SIM and No Service? No SIM: device doesn't detect a SIM card at all. No Service: device sees the SIM but can't register on a network. Both require board-level diagnosis. Can carrier unlocking fix a No SIM problem? No — carrier unlocking is a software state. If the device can't detect any SIM at all, it's a hardware fault that unlocking cannot fix. My iPhone 17 Air shows No SIM — I was told it's eSIM only? Correct. The 17 Air is eSIM only — no physical SIM slot. If it shows No SIM, the eSIM profile may need re-provisioning with your carrier, or there is a hardware eSIM fault. Contact your carrier first. Does Taptic Engine failure affect other functions? Yes — keyboard click sensation, Haptic Touch feedback, and haptic notifications are all absent. If haptics are globally absent across all interactions, Taptic Engine failure is confirmed. Can a Taptic Engine be repaired? The Taptic Engine is not serviceable at component level — replaced as a complete unit. Sometimes a disconnected flex cable causes the same symptoms. We check the connector first. Wi-Fi after liquid damage Liquid ingress near the WLAN module is a common damage pattern. Board clean and module assessment before replacement. No. Wi-Fi greyed out is a hardware fault. No software reset, iOS restore, or factory reset resolves a hardware Wi-Fi fault. Micro-soldering board repair is required. My iPhone Bluetooth has completely disappeared from Settings — what is that? Wi-Fi and Bluetooth share the same chip on iPhones. When the chip or board connections fail, both can disappear simultaneously. One micro-soldering repair restores both. My iPhone 12 Mini shows No SIM and no Wi-Fi after a drop — are those related? Yes — both are caused by the same AP/RF board solder joint failure. The 12 Mini's compact board flexes more than other 12 series models. One board-level reball typically resolves both faults. Can a Wi-Fi fault be caused by the antenna, not the chip? Yes — loose antenna connections can cause weak or absent Wi-Fi. We check antenna connections first. If antennas are intact and Wi-Fi is still greyed out, the chip or solder joints are the fault. My iPhone's Wi-Fi range is much shorter than it used to be — is that a fault? Reduced range can indicate a partially damaged RF chip or loose antenna connection. Antenna cleaning or re-seating sometimes resolves range issues before chip-level repair is needed. Will a factory reset fix greyed-out Wi-Fi? No. Factory reset removes data — it doesn't repair hardware. If Wi-Fi is greyed out before the reset, it will be greyed out after. How long does Wi-Fi / Bluetooth repair take? Board removal, inspection, reball, and testing: typically same-day. Is Wi-Fi greyed out covered under warranty? Physical damage is not covered under Apple's standard warranty. years At eight years old, iPhone X batteries are severely degraded. Most units are at 60–70% health — well below Apple's 80% threshold. Throttling is aggressive, daily battery life is very short, and unexpected shutdowns at 20–30% are common. Battery replacement is the single most impactful repair on this device. Check Settings → Battery → Battery Health. Same-day replacement at our Silvamonte centre. ⚠ OLED burn-in — common at 8 years The first-generation iPhone OLED panel in the iPhone X is showing significant burn-in on heavily used devices at this age. The most common patterns: a faint ghost of the status bar visible on white backgrounds, keyboard ghost at the bottom of the screen, and home indicator ghost. Burn-in is a permanent change to the OLED organic compounds and cannot be corrected by software or settings. Screen replacement with a new or used original OLED resolves it. Glass-only refurbishment is available where the panel is working but burn-in is minimal. ⚠ Touch failure after drops — Meson touch IC fault The iPhone X has a known touch fault pattern after drop impacts. The Meson touch IC on the logic board manages all touch input from the OLED digitiser. The Meson chip uses Ball Grid Array (BGA) solder connections. When the iPhone X is dropped — especially on a hard surface — the impact can cause the BGA solder balls underneath the Meson chip to crack or lose contact with the board. The result is partial or complete loss of touch response that a new screen does not fix. Key diagnostic clue: If a brand new replacement screen shows the same touch problem as the original — no touch, intermittent touch, or ghost touches — the fault is the Meson IC on the board, not the screen. The repair: The Meson IC is removed under microscope, the board pads are cleaned of the original lead-free solder (which is more brittle than leaded solder and prone to this failure), and the chip is reballed and resoldered with fresh balls. Where the chip itself is damaged, a replacement Meson is fitted. If your iPhone X lost touch after a drop and a screen replacement did not fix it — the Meson IC is almost certainly the cause. Bring it in for a free board-level diagnostic. ⚠ Face ID / TrueDepth — JCID repair, R1,500 if fixable The iPhone X has the first-generation TrueDepth camera. Face ID failures are common at this age — from earpiece flex degradation, TrueDepth connector corrosion, or component failure. We use the JCID tag on flex method to restore Face ID where the fault is a repairable component. If the IR camera has failed, Face ID cannot be recovered — we diagnose specifically and advise before any charge. Price: R1,500 if repairable via JCID method. No charge if IR camera failure means Face ID is unrecoverable. ⚠ Hydra charging IC — Lightning charging fault at this age Eight years of cheap Lightning cable use takes its toll on the Hydra charging IC. Won't charge on Lightning while wireless charging continues — 80% Hydra IC, 20% Lightning port. Free diagnostic confirms which. Charges wirelessly but not via Lightning? ~80% Hydra IC, ~20% Lightning port. Use Apple MFi-certified cables only. ⚠ NAND storage failure — stuck in iTunes mode, slow performance, micro-soldering repair After eight years of daily read and write operations, the NAND flash storage chip on the iPhone 8 and iPhone X logic board is increasingly showing wear-related failure. The NAND is the chip that stores iOS, all your apps, photos, messages, and every piece of data on the device. Unlike SSDs in computers, smartphone NAND chips have a finite number of write cycles — and after 8 years of intensive use, many are worn to the point of developing bad blocks, degraded write speeds, and read errors that the bootloader cannot tolerate. Common symptoms of NAND wear on the iPhone 8 and X: Stuck in iTunes / recovery mode — the iPhone enters recovery mode (lightning cable and iTunes/Finder logo on screen) and cannot complete a restore. iTunes or Finder shows error codes 4013, 9, 14, or 21 during the restore attempt. The restore starts, the progress bar appears, then fails. This is one of the clearest indicators of a NAND timing issue — the bootloader cannot read or write to the chip fast enough to complete the iOS installation. Extremely slow performance — even with a brand new battery fitted, the device is inexplicably slow. Apps take 30–60 seconds to open. Every operation involves long waits. This is the NAND struggling to serve read requests at speed. Bootloop that does not resolve with a software restore — the device restarts continuously and DFU restore fails or produces the same error codes repeatedly. Data corruption — apps crash, the OS itself becomes unstable, files become unreadable. The repair — NAND chip replacement (micro-soldering): The original NAND chip must be removed under microscope, the board pads cleaned, and a replacement NAND chip programmed and installed. This requires not just soldering skill but also the ability to correctly program the new chip with the device's unique identifiers (serial number, Wi-Fi address, and baseband data) that are stored on the original NAND. Without correct programming the device will not activate. This is one of the most complex board-level repairs available. Our recommendation when replacing NAND — upgrade to 256GB: If your iPhone 8 or iPhone X is having its NAND replaced, we strongly recommend taking the opportunity to upgrade the storage to 256GB at the same time. The cost of the NAND chip itself is the primary expense — and since the board is already open and the micro-soldering work is already being performed, upgrading from 64GB or 128GB to 256GB adds minimal extra cost relative to the total repair. The result is a device with significantly more storage capacity and a fresh NAND chip with maximum remaining write cycles — effectively extending the useful life of the device considerably. If your iPhone 8 or iPhone X is stuck in iTunes mode and restore keeps failing — bring it in for a free board diagnostic. We assess the NAND, discuss the repair options and the 256GB upgrade, and quote before any work begins. quote Known issues on the iPhone XR — read before booking ⚠ Battery degradation — critical at 7 years At seven years old, battery replacement is no longer optional for most users. Seven years of daily charge cycles leaves most batteries well below Apple's 80% service threshold — and many at 65–75%. At this level, iOS performance throttling is fully active, daily battery life is significantly shorter, and unexpected shutdowns at 15–30% charge are common. Check Settings → Battery → Battery Health. Below 80% is Apple's service recommendation. Same-day battery replacement available at our Silvamonte centre. Battery replacement restores full capacity, removes throttling, and transforms daily performance on these devices. ⚠ Hydra charging IC failure — Lightning charging fault at this age The Hydra IC manages all Lightning charging communication on this generation. After 7 years of cheap uncertified cable use or power surges, failure is increasingly common. Symptoms: "This accessory may not be supported", won't charge on Lightning but works wirelessly, won't appear in iTunes/Finder, slow charging. Charges wirelessly but not via Lightning? ~80% Hydra IC, ~20% Lightning port. Free diagnostic confirms which before any work begins. Micro-soldering repair. Use only Apple MFi-certified Lightning cables to prevent Hydra IC damage. ⚠ Face ID / TrueDepth camera — JCID repair, R1,500 if fixable We use the JCID tag on flex method to repair TrueDepth camera faults and restore Face ID where the fault is a repairable component. If the IR camera itself has failed — cryptographically paired at the factory — Face ID cannot be recovered. We diagnose this specifically and advise before charging anything. Price: R1,500 if repairable. No charge for diagnostic if it turns out to be the IR camera. ⚠ Random rebooting every 3 minutes — thermalmonitord panic, R250 diagnostic The thermalmonitord sensor-detection reboot pattern applies to this model. The device reboots every 2–3 minutes when a required sensor loses communication. The panic log shows: "Missing sensor(s): Prs0" (barometric sensor on the charging port flex) or "Missing sensor(s): mic2" (secondary microphone on the power button flex). Both are easily damaged by drops, cracked back glass, or back glass laser repairs. OEM pull parts required — cheap aftermarket flexes frequently lack the sensors. R250 diagnostic — panic log read first, credited against repair cost. Software restore does nothing for a hardware sensor bootloop. Bring it in for a panic log diagnostic. ⚠ NAND storage failure — stuck in iTunes / DFU mode, P15 programmer repair The iPhone XR is now at an age where NAND flash storage wear is a regular repair we see. The NAND chip stores iOS, all apps, photos, and data — and after years of daily read and write operations, worn sectors and degraded write speeds cause failures that look like software problems but are not. What many shops get wrong: When a device is stuck in iTunes or DFU mode with restore failing, most shops attempt repeated DFU restores — sometimes charging for a "software repair" — without diagnosing the actual NAND hardware fault. A NAND failure cannot be resolved by any software restore. The restore fails because the NAND chip cannot complete the write process reliably. Symptoms: Stuck in iTunes / recovery mode with error codes 4013, 9, 14, or 21 during restore. DFU restore loop that always fails. Inexplicably slow performance even with a new battery. Bootloop that software cannot resolve. The repair: We use the P15 NAND programmer to replace and correctly program the NAND chip — including the device's unique serial number, Wi-Fi address, and baseband data. Without correct programming the device will not activate after NAND replacement. Upgrade to 256GB recommended: Since the board is open and the micro-soldering work is already being performed, we recommend upgrading to 256GB at the same time. Fresh chip, maximum write cycles remaining, significantly more storage — for minimal additional cost over the base NAND replacement. If your iPhone XR is stuck in iTunes or DFU mode and restore keeps failing — bring it in for a free board-level diagnostic before spending more time on software restores that will not work. Over time — from age, heat cycles, or drops — these solder joints crack or lose contact, disrupting the touch digitiser signal path. This restores the electrical connection and full touchscreen function. We perform this regularly on the XS and XS Max. WhatsApp For A Quote Call 078 742 4769 ⚠ No touch / unresponsive touchscreen — interposer solder fault One of the most distinctive known faults on the iPhone XS and XS Max is a complete or partial loss of touchscreen response — not caused by screen damage, but by failing solder joints on the motherboard interposer . The XS and XS Max use a two-layer sandwich logic board. The upper and lower boards connect via a grid of small solder balls. Over time — from age, heat cycles, or drops — these solder joints crack or lose contact, disrupting the touch digitiser signal path. Touchscreen completely unresponsive — screen lights up correctly but registers no touch Touch works intermittently — responds sometimes but fails randomly Dead zones in specific areas of the screen Touch failure appeared after a drop or hot environment exposure A replacement screen makes no difference — the fault is in the board, not the display The repair — interposer reball: We remove the old solder balls between the two board layers, clean the pads, apply fresh solder balls, and reflow under microscope. This restores the electrical connection and full touchscreen function. We perform this regularly on the XS and XS Max. If a replacement screen did not fix your touch issue, the interposer is almost certainly the cause. Bring it in for a free diagnostic. Ready to fix your iPhone XS? The NAND chip stores iOS, all apps, photos, and data — and after years of daily read and write operations, worn sectors and degraded write speeds cause failures that look like software problems but are not. What many shops get wrong: When a device is stuck in iTunes or DFU mode with restore failing, most shops attempt repeated DFU restores — sometimes charging for a "software repair" — without diagnosing the actual NAND hardware fault. A NAND failure cannot be resolved by any software restore. Error codes 4013, 9, 14, or 21 during restore point directly to NAND. The repair: We use the P15 NAND programmer to replace and correctly program the NAND — including the device's unique serial number, Wi-Fi address, and baseband data. Joy-Con 2 repairs are quoted after a free check. What causes Joy-Con drift? The analogue stick uses contacts that rub across a track every time you move it. Over time they wear and dust gets in, so the stick reports a direction even when it's centred. It's normal wear, sped up by heavy play — not something you did wrong. Can I fix Joy-Con drift myself? Updating the controllers and recalibrating the sticks in System Settings is worth trying first, and it sometimes helps for a while. If the drift keeps coming back, the stick module is worn and needs replacing. What is a Hall Effect stick? It's a replacement stick that measures position with magnets and a sensor instead of contacts rubbing on a track. Because nothing rubs, there's nothing to wear down, so it doesn't drift the same way. It fits inside the original Joy-Con and works with every game. Is it cheaper to repair or buy new Joy-Cons? Repairing is usually much cheaper. A drift repair costs a fraction of a new pair of Joy-Cons, and new Joy-Cons use the same kind of stick, so they can drift again too. A Hall Effect upgrade fixes the cause. Do I need to bring my Switch? Not for an original Joy-Con or a Joy-Con 2 — just bring the controller that drifts. For a Switch Lite, the sticks are built in, so bring the console. Do original Joy-Cons work on the Switch 2? They can pair with a Switch 2 wirelessly, but they don't attach to it. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Common questions Mac mini logic board repair — FAQ My Mac mini won't turn on at all — is that the logic board or power supply? A completely unresponsive Mac mini is most often a power supply fault, a blown capacitor on the logic board power rail, or surge damage from load-shedding. Our technicians run a full board-level diagnostic to isolate the exact fault. A common quick test: if the power LED does not illuminate at all, suspect the PSU first. Free diagnostic confirms the fault before any quote. My Mac mini powers on but gives no display output — what is the fault? No display output with the Mac mini otherwise running (fan spinning, startup sound) is almost always a port fault or GPU signal fault on the logic board — not the display itself. Test with a different cable and a different monitor first. If both fail, bring it in for a free diagnostic. Thunderbolt controller IC faults are repairable at component level on all Intel Mac mini models. Can you repair Mac mini M1, M2, and M4 logic boards? Yes — M-series Mac mini logic board repairs are performed at chip level. Apple Silicon integrates CPU, GPU, RAM, and Neural Engine into a single package, making standard part-swap approaches impossible. iAssist diagnoses M-series board faults at component level, targeting the specific failed circuit. My Mac mini 2018 shuts down randomly under load — what causes that? Random shutdowns under load on the 2018 Mac mini are most commonly caused by a failing power supply unable to sustain current draw, degraded thermal paste causing thermal protection shutdowns, or a power management IC fault on the logic board. An SMC reset is worth trying first — unplug for 15 seconds, replug, wait 5 seconds, power on. If shutdowns continue, bring it in. Will my data be safe during logic board repair? Yes. Component-level board repair does not involve the storage drive. Your data stays completely intact throughout. If the fault has caused storage failure we advise you separately on data recovery options before any other repair work begins. How long does Mac mini logic board repair take? Board-level diagnostic is completed same day. Component-level repair typically takes 1–3 business days depending on fault complexity. Board replacement (where required) takes 3–5 days including parts sourcing. We give you a clear timeline upfront and update you throughout. Do you offer collection for Mac mini logic board repair? Yes — R300 insured door-to-door collection and return across Gauteng. The Mac mini is compact and easy to package for courier. WhatsApp us on 078 742 4769 to arrange pickup. My Mac mini 2014 or 2012 crashes constantly — is it the logic board? Frequent crashes on older Mac mini models are usually caused by failing storage (SSD or HDD), insufficient RAM for the running macOS version, or degraded thermal paste causing overheating. A failing logic board is possible but less common than storage or thermal faults. We diagnose all three during the free assessment. My Mac mini 2018 passes diagnostics but still crashes — what could cause that? The 2018 Mac mini occasionally develops intermittent NAND storage faults that pass standard diagnostics but cause random crashes under sustained read/write operations. We run extended storage stress tests alongside board diagnostics to catch these. A failing T2 chip can also cause intermittent instability — diagnosable at component level. Can load-shedding damage a Mac mini that was turned off at the time? Yes — even a powered-off Mac mini remains connected to the mains if plugged in, and the power supply is still exposed to the surge. The standby circuits and PSU capacitors can absorb surge damage even without the machine being active. The Mac mini 2012 has two SO-DIMM slots accessible via the bottom panel — easy upgrade up to 16GB DDR3. The Mac mini 2018 has SO-DIMM slots but they require significant internal disassembly including logic board extraction to access — upgradeable up to 64GB DDR4. The Mac mini 2014 has RAM permanently soldered to the logic board — not upgradeable. M1, M2, and M4 Mac minis use Unified Memory integrated into the Apple Silicon chip — not upgradeable. How much does Mac mini RAM upgrade cost? iAssist charges R1,600 per 8GB module. The 2012 Mac mini uses DDR3 1600MHz SO-DIMMs. The 2018 uses DDR4 2666MHz SO-DIMMs. Configuration is confirmed before ordering to ensure correct speed matching for your specific model. Is the Mac mini 2018 RAM upgrade worth doing given the disassembly required? For many users, yes. The 2018 Mac mini base model ships with 8GB which is insufficient for modern workloads. Upgrading to 16GB or 32GB makes a significant difference in responsiveness, especially with multiple apps or browser tabs open. The full disassembly required adds labour cost but the upgrade is reliable and carries a 6-month warranty. My Mac mini 2014 is slow — can I upgrade the RAM? No. The Mac mini 2014 has RAM permanently soldered to the logic board. No upgrade is possible. If the machine is slow, an SSD upgrade will make the biggest difference — the 2014 uses a proprietary PCIe SSD that can be replaced with a faster drive. How do I know if I need more RAM on my Mac mini? Open Activity Monitor, click the Memory tab, and look at Memory Pressure and Swap Used. If Memory Pressure is yellow or red, or Swap Used is above zero, more RAM will make a clear difference. If both look fine, the bottleneck is more likely storage — an SSD will have more impact than RAM in that case. How long does Mac mini RAM upgrade take? 2012 models are completed in under 1 hour — the bottom panel removal is quick. 2018 models require 2–3 hours due to full internal disassembly. We give you a clear timeline when you drop the machine off. Do you offer collection for Mac mini RAM upgrades? Yes — R300 door-to-door collection and return across Gauteng. WhatsApp us on 078 742 4769 to arrange pickup. Can I add RAM to my existing sticks or must I replace all of them? On the 2012 Mac mini you can add matched pairs to empty slots without replacing existing sticks, provided the new modules match the speed of the existing ones. On the 2018 you have two slots — we check your current configuration before ordering to ensure matching. Do I need to upgrade RAM and SSD at the same time on the Mac mini 2012? Not necessarily, but it makes financial sense if you are already opening the machine. The 2012 RAM is accessible via the bottom panel with no tools — the quickest Mac RAM upgrade available. If you also want an SSD, that requires deeper disassembly regardless. Doing both in one visit saves on labour if the SSD job is also being done. Known Mac mini issues Every Mac mini generation eventually develops a personality — usually expressed through a specific design fault that turns up like clockwork after a few years of use. Below are the ones we see most often on the workshop bench. None is terminal. Each has a well-defined repair path and we've handled all of them many times over. Mac mini 2023 · M2 "No Power" — Apple's official service program Apple has confirmed that a small percentage of 2023 M2 Mac minis manufactured between June 2024 and November 2024 may fail to power on. Apple covers the repair free of charge for up to three years from the original purchase date — check your serial number on Apple's Mac mini Service Program page first. If your machine doesn't qualify (different production date, expired three-year window, or unrelated power fault), it's still fixable — board-level power issues are exactly the kind of work we do. iAssist fix: Component-level power-rail diagnosis and repair via micro-soldering. Original board preserved, integrated SSD and data kept intact. Mac mini 2018 · A1993 HDMI port instability The 2018 Intel Mac mini has a widely-reported pattern of HDMI signal drops — black screen on boot, "no signal" until you cycle the monitor, sporadic disconnects after macOS updates. Some cases are resolved by SMC/NVRAM resets or different cables, but persistent faults usually point to the HDMI controller circuit on the logic board. Workarounds via Thunderbolt-to-HDMI adapters work but cost you a port — the proper fix restores native HDMI output. iAssist fix: Free diagnostic to separate software from hardware causes. Board-level HDMI controller repair where the fault is hardware. Mac mini Intel · 2018 i7 in particular Fan noise & thermal throttling The 2018 Mac mini's i7-8700B is a 65W chip squeezed into a tiny aluminium chassis. Under any sustained load — compiling, encoding video, multitasking — the fan spins up to maximum and stays there. Over time, dust accumulation makes it worse, and dried thermal paste pushes CPU temperatures high enough to cause throttling and shorten chip lifespan. An aggressive fan and a constantly-warm chassis are not normal "wear and tear" — they're a maintenance issue with a fix. iAssist fix: Internal teardown, dust removal, fan service, and fresh high-conductivity thermal paste. Temperatures typically drop 15-25°C and fan behaviour returns to normal. Known issues with this model Common MacBook Air 11-inch A1465 / A1370 faults we see Liquid damage — extremely vulnerable design The 11-inch MacBook Air's small chassis concentrates the logic board directly beneath the keyboard with almost no clearance. Even a few drops of liquid on the keyboard reach the board almost immediately. The bottom air intake then draws in residual moisture. Corrosion on the charging circuit, MagSafe connector, and USB ports is the most common result — often appearing weeks after the initial spill. Board-level micro-soldering is required, not just a clean. MagSafe port failure The 11-inch models use MagSafe 1 (A1370) or MagSafe 2 (A1465). A swelling battery pushes up the trackpad and bottom case visibly. Stop using immediately — fire risk. Battery replacement is straightforward on these models (no adhesive pull tabs on A1370/A1465 — screwed in). Display hinge damage — thin lid cracks easily The 11-inch display lid is thin and vulnerable to cracking near the hinge from being closed with objects underneath, or from being dropped at the hinge line. A cracked lid assembly requires full display replacement — a replacement lid assembly covers the full lid. Slow performance — RAM not upgradeable All 11-inch MacBook Airs have soldered RAM. 2GB models from 2010-2012 are extremely slow on any modern macOS. 4GB is borderline; 8GB is comfortable. OCLP allows Sonoma installation on 2013-2015 A1465 models — an SSD upgrade combined with OCLP gives these machines genuinely useful performance at low cost. A failed jack — from wear, liquid ingress, or debris — is fixed by replacing the I/O board. Much cheaper than a logic board replacement. Audio stuck routing through headphones — speakers silent A classic symptom of a dirty or failed headphone jack sensor. The Mac thinks headphones are connected and routes audio away from the internal speakers permanently. Compressed air in the jack sometimes resolves it — if not, the jack sensor has failed and I/O board replacement is required. Microphone not working — Zoom, Teams, voice memos silent On Intel MacBook Airs (A1466, A1932, A2179, A2337) the microphone array is near the keyboard or on the I/O board. A failed I/O board, broken flex cable, or corrosion from liquid ingress causes total microphone failure. On M-series models the microphone is inside the display assembly — fault diagnosis differs. Microphone picks up only one side or has poor quality Partial microphone failure — one microphone capsule in the array has failed. The Mac uses multiple microphone capsules for noise cancellation. A failed capsule degrades audio quality even if recording still works. I/O board replacement restores full multi-mic performance. I/O board flex cable damaged or frayed The ribbon cable connecting the I/O board to the logic board is routed across a high-stress path inside the chassis. Repeated opening and closing fatigues the cable over years of use. A broken flex cable kills the headphone jack, microphone, and MagSafe indicator simultaneously. Flex cable and I/O board replacement. No MagSafe LED — port works but light is dead On A1466 models the MagSafe LED indicator is controlled by the I/O board. USB-C charging failure on MacBook Air is overwhelmingly a USB-C power delivery controller IC fault on the logic board rather than physical port damage. The port itself is soldered to the board, but the controller IC governing power delivery can fail independently. Component-level IC replacement restores full charging function in most cases without board replacement. My MacBook Air MagSafe 3 port is not charging — what should I try first? Try a different MagSafe 3 cable and charger first — cable failure is common. Also try a USB-C charger in one of the Thunderbolt ports to isolate whether the fault is MagSafe-specific or board-level. My MacBook Air charges intermittently — works sometimes, not others — what is that? Under any sustained load the Core i5 hits 90–100°C and macOS throttles performance. Thermal paste replacement plus copper shim installation reduces temperatures by 20–30°C and significantly reduces or eliminates throttling. Fan running at full speed constantly Fan stuck at maximum speed despite a cool or idle machine usually indicates a failed temperature sensor — most commonly the battery thermistor. The SMC runs the fan at max when it cannot read temperature. Apple Diagnostics error codes PPT006 or PFM006 confirm this. Battery replacement resolves most cases. Fan grinding or rattling noise Bearing wear inside the fan causes grinding or clicking at certain RPMs. A failing fan bearing cannot be repaired — fan replacement required. A seized fan leaves the machine with no cooling at all. Fan not spinning A fan that doesn't spin causes rapid CPU temperature rise and emergency shutdown. Causes: failed fan motor, broken cable, or board fault on the fan power rail. MacBook Air hot on palm rest or bottom Excessive chassis heat on A1466 models is usually dried thermal paste — 5+ year old machines often have paste that has hardened and cracked. Thermal paste replacement restores normal temperatures. Machine sluggish under any load The CPU throttle cycle: fan ramps up, CPU cools, macOS releases throttle, CPU heats again, cycle repeats. Small spills — even a few drops of coffee or tea — get drawn straight into the logic board. Corrosion is often delayed: the machine works fine for days or weeks then dies suddenly as oxidation spreads across power rails and SMC circuits. The MagSafe I/O board cable area, charging circuit (ISL6259), and trackpad connector traces are the most common failure points. Micro-soldering repair or component-level board work is required — not just a clean. MagSafe port not charging The MagSafe 2 I/O board and its ribbon cable are a weak point. Corrosion from minor liquid ingress, cable fraying at the hinge, or physical damage to the port pins causes the charger light to stay green permanently or not light at all. Often misdiagnosed as a dead battery. I/O board and cable replacement resolves most cases. Won't turn on — fan spins briefly then stops Classic symptom of a failed or short-circuited power rail, often from previous liquid damage or a blown fuse on the board. The fan spin-and-stop with no display indicates power is reaching the fan but the SMC can't complete POST. Requires board-level diagnostics to identify the failed component. USB-A ports intermittent or dead USB ports share a rail with the I/O board. Port failure is often caused by corrosion on the I/O board connector, a blown USB power fuse on the logic board, or physical damage from a forced connection. Component-level repair or I/O board replacement. Display backlight fails — dark screen with faint image Shine a torch at the screen at an angle — if you can see a faint desktop, the backlight has failed. Common causes: blown backlight fuse (F7700 or similar), failed backlight IC (U7701), or corroded LVDS cable connector from liquid entry. Logic board micro-soldering repair in most cases. Keyboard and trackpad stop working after spill The keyboard and trackpad share a ribbon cable that routes across a vulnerable path inside the A1466. Even small spills cause SMC resets on every power button press (a sign the keyboard matrix is shorted). Topcase replacement plus board inspection required — the board may be developing further corrosion. Stop using that cable immediately and try a different MagSafe 2 charger. If the problem persists with a different cable, bring it in for a free diagnostic of the charging port. Constant fan on a MacBook Air that is not under load usually indicates dried thermal paste causing the CPU to run hotter than it should. The CD3217 is a Texas Instruments USB-C power delivery controller IC — when it fails the machine is completely dead: no charging light, no fan spin, no response to any input. It's frequently misdiagnosed as a dead battery or dead charger. iAssist identifies and replaces failed CD3217 chips at component level under microscope. This is a micro-soldering repair, not a board replacement — significantly cheaper than a new logic board and it's a recognised fix with a high success rate on these models. Severe thermal throttling — no proper heatsink The A1932 and A2179 are notorious for Apple's thermal design: the CPU fan is not aimed directly at the processor heatsink. Under any sustained load — video calls, multiple browser tabs, PDF rendering — the i5 core temperatures climb to 90–100°C and macOS throttles the CPU below its base clock to prevent damage. This is a design limitation, not a fixable fault. Thermal paste replacement and copper shim installation can reduce temperatures by 20–30°C and delay throttling significantly. iAssist performs this service as part of fan/thermal servicing. CPU failure from sustained heat Years of thermal stress degrades the Intel Core i5 die. The A1932 and A2179 logic boards fail more frequently than any other modern MacBook Air. Symptoms: random kernel panics, failure to boot, black screen after POST, or the machine runs but throttles immediately to minimal performance. Logic board replacement is the only fix — component-level CPU reballing is not practical on these models. A1932 butterfly keyboard failure The A1932 uses Apple's butterfly keyboard mechanism — the same defective design from the 2016–2019 MacBook Pro range. Keys ghost, repeat, or stop responding entirely. Apple's free repair programme has ended. iAssist offers keyboard-only or full topcase replacement. The A2179 (2020) switched to the scissor mechanism and does not have this issue. USB-C port failure — only two ports, one side often dies The A1932 has only two Thunderbolt 3 USB-C ports. The charging port IC (USB-C board) fails due to heat, liquid, or damaged cables being forced in. With one port dead, charging options are severely limited. USB-C board replacement is a component-level repair iAssist handles regularly. Fan running at full speed constantly A failed temperature sensor — most commonly the battery thermistor — causes the SMC to run the fan at maximum as a safety response. Often triggered by liquid damage or a degraded battery. Diagnostics show PFM006 or PPT006 error codes via Apple Diagnostics. Battery replacement resolves the majority of cases. Display backlight dim or dead on one side The A1932 retina display backlight circuit is sensitive to voltage spikes. A blown backlight fuse or failed driver IC produces a dim screen, bright spots on one edge, or total backlight failure. Micro-soldering board repair in most cases. Display assembly replacement if the panel itself is damaged. Yes — topcase replacement is the correct fix for butterfly keyboard failure on the A1932. This is a known Apple manufacturing defect. Can I upgrade the SSD on my 2018, 2019, or 2020 Intel MacBook Air? No — all three models (A1932 and A2179) have SSDs soldered to the logic board. No upgrade is possible. External Thunderbolt storage is the only option for expanding capacity. My 2018 MacBook Air has a T2 chip — what does that mean for repairs? The T2 chip encrypts all storage and ties the encryption keys to that specific logic board. If the board fails, data cannot be recovered by connecting the drive to another machine — the original board must be restored. iAssist always attempts board restoration before declaring data unrecoverable. The 2018/2019 MacBook Air Touch ID fingerprint scanner stopped working — is that the board? Touch ID on the MacBook Air is paired to the Secure Enclave on the logic board. Disconnect the charger immediately. Turn the MacBook Air upside down in an inverted V shape to let excess liquid drain away from the logic board. Do not use rice or a hairdryer — neither removes corrosive mineral deposits. Contact us immediately. The faster treatment begins, the higher the recovery rate. My MacBook Air worked after getting wet but now it is dead — what happened? This is the most common pattern with liquid damage. The machine works initially because the liquid hasn't bridged critical circuits yet. As it dries it leaves conductive mineral deposits that progressively short more circuits. A MacBook Air that fails days or weeks after a liquid event is corrosion completing its work — bring it in immediately. How much does MacBook Air liquid damage repair cost? Liquid damage repair ranges from R900 to R2,800 depending on the extent of corrosion and which components are affected. The diagnostic and ultrasonic clean is performed first, after which we confirm the repair scope in writing. You decide before any further work begins. Can you recover data from a liquid-damaged MacBook Air? In most cases yes. On Intel models without T2 chip (2013–2017), the SSD blade can often be read on external equipment independently. On T2-encrypted models (2018–2020) and M-series, the storage is tied to the logic board and recovery requires board restoration. We always attempt data recovery before any repair work. What liquid types cause the most damage to MacBook Air? Sugary drinks (Coke, juice, coffee with sugar) cause the most aggressive corrosion due to highly conductive sugar residue. Black coffee or plain water cause less corrosion but still require proper ultrasonic treatment. All liquid types require professional cleaning — wiping the board is insufficient. Do I need to bring the charger as well? Yes — bring the charger cable. We test the charging circuit separately as part of the liquid damage assessment, and the charger may also have been affected. How long does MacBook Air liquid damage repair take? Ultrasonic cleaning and assessment: 1–2 business days. Component repair following assessment: 1–3 further days. Yes — R300 insured door-to-door collection across Gauteng. Keep the machine off and disconnected until collected. WhatsApp us on 078 742 4769 for urgent pickup. My MacBook Air keys are sticky after a spill but the machine works — should I still bring it in? Yes — sticky keys after a spill mean liquid has entered the keyboard and is leaving corrosive residue. In many cases the fix is a single IC replacement, not a full board swap. What is component-level logic board repair? Component-level repair means identifying and replacing the specific failed chip, capacitor, resistor, or trace on the logic board — rather than replacing the entire board. iAssist uses microscope-assisted micro-soldering to replace individual components. This is typically 30–70% cheaper than a board replacement and is the preferred approach on all MacBook Air models. My MacBook Air has liquid damage — is the logic board repairable? Yes in most cases. Liquid damage causes corrosion on specific components rather than destroying the whole board. iAssist performs ultrasonic board cleaning followed by component-level diagnosis and replacement of damaged ICs, capacitors, and resistors. Bring it in immediately — every hour the machine sits powered off reduces further corrosion damage. What is the CD3217 chip and why does it fail? The CD3217B12 and CD3217B13 are Texas Instruments USB-C power delivery controller ICs used on A1932, A2179, and A2337 MacBook Airs. When they fail — from voltage spikes, heat, or faulty cables — the machine is completely dead with no charging light. Component-level IC replacement under microscope resolves this. High success rate. Can data be recovered from a dead logic board? On Intel MacBook Airs the SSD is a removable blade — it can be extracted and read via a USB adapter even if the logic board is completely dead. On M-series models the SSD is soldered and encrypted, requiring micro-soldering to restore the power path before recovery. iAssist handles both scenarios. Complex liquid damage repairs involving multiple components take 2–5 days. iAssist provides a realistic timeline at the diagnostic stage. What if the logic board cannot be repaired? If component-level repair is not feasible, iAssist will advise on board replacement options or help with data recovery before the machine is retired. We do not charge for diagnostic work if the machine is beyond economic repair. Does logic board repair carry a warranty? Yes — iAssist provides a 6-month warranty on all logic board component repairs. No. The M1 MacBook Air (A2337) has Unified Memory and SSD storage both integrated into the Apple M1 chip package. Neither can be upgraded after purchase. Is the MacBook Air M1 still worth repairing in 2025? Absolutely — the M1 MacBook Air is one of the best value computers ever made. My MacBook Air M1 battery drains very fast — how long should it last? The M1 MacBook Air is rated at up to 18 hours. Under normal use (web, documents, email) 12–14 hours is typical. The MacBook Air M1 does not have a fan — is that a problem for intensive tasks? Under sustained heavy loads the M1 will throttle performance to manage heat. For everyday computing the M1 Air is outstanding. My MacBook Air M1 keyboard has a key that stopped working — what options do I have? Under sustained CPU or GPU workloads — video export, extended gaming, large Xcode builds — the M2 throttles performance to manage temperature. For light to moderate daily use this is rarely noticeable, but professionals pushing the chip find it limiting. The only solution is the MacBook Pro which has active cooling. Base 256GB model — slow SSD speeds A known hardware limitation: the 256GB M2 MacBook Air uses a single NAND chip, while 512GB and above use two chips in parallel. Real-world sequential write speeds on the 256GB model are significantly lower than Apple's published figures. This affects large file transfers, video editing scratch disk performance, and Time Machine backups. Upgrading the SSD is not possible — the storage is soldered. Buy 512GB or above if storage-intensive tasks are planned. MagSafe 3 port not charging The MagSafe 3 port introduced on the M2 is a new failure point. Physical damage, lint compaction, or a bent pin in the port stops charging. In some cases the USB-C ports continue to charge normally — use these as a workaround while the MagSafe port is repaired. MagSafe 3 socket replacement is a board-level micro-soldering repair. Display backlight failure The M2 Liquid Retina display backlight circuit can fail from voltage irregularities or physical impact. A dim screen or total backlight loss (image visible with torch) typically requires display assembly replacement — the M2 display is not repairable at panel level. Touch ID not working after topcase replacement Same as M1 — Touch ID is paired to the Secure Enclave. Any topcase or keyboard replacement breaks the pairing. Apple Configurator re-pairing is required post-repair. iAssist advises this before any topcase work is carried out. Liquid damage — soldered SSD makes recovery harder The M2 has a soldered SSD with hardware encryption tied to the Secure Enclave. Liquid damage that kills the logic board also locks the data. Micro-soldering is required to restore the power path. Data recovery from a dead M2 board is possible but difficult — bring it in immediately without powering on after a spill. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Common questions MacBook Air M2 Repair — FAQ Can the RAM or SSD be upgraded on the MacBook Air M2? No. Both Unified Memory and SSD are integrated into the M2 chip package. The MacBook Air M2 starts at 8GB RAM — for heavy workloads configure 16GB at purchase. No upgrade path exists after the fact. My MacBook Air M2 screen has a notch — does that affect repairability? The M2 MacBook Air was the first Air with a display notch (housing the webcam). The display assembly is replaced as a complete unit. The notch does not significantly affect the repair approach but the M2 display assembly is colour-specific (Midnight, Starlight, Silver, Space Grey) — confirm your colour before ordering. What is the difference between the 13-inch (A2681) and 15-inch (A2941) for repairs? The 13-inch A2681 uses the standard M2 chip. The 15-inch A2941 uses the same M2 chip in a larger chassis. Display assemblies, topcase, and batteries are different parts between the two. Logic board repairs use the same approach. Always confirm your exact model identifier. My MacBook Air M2 is not charging through MagSafe but charges through USB-C — what does that mean? This isolates the fault to the MagSafe controller circuit specifically, not the broader USB-C charging system. MagSafe 3 controller IC repair restores full MagSafe function. Bring it in for a free diagnostic. The MacBook Air M2 15-inch runs warm during sustained tasks — is that normal? Yes — the MacBook Air is fanless. The 15-inch M2 has more thermal mass to dissipate heat, but sustained heavy tasks will cause the machine to throttle. If it's warm during normal everyday tasks like browsing or documents, that suggests a board-level fault. Free diagnostic to assess. Can you repair the webcam on a MacBook Air M2? The webcam (1080p FaceTime HD) on the M2 MacBook Air is part of the display assembly. Webcam failure usually means display assembly replacement. Free diagnostic to confirm before quoting. My MacBook Air M2 dropped and the casing is dented — can that be repaired? The aluminium body denting is cosmetic. We repair functional faults — if the drop also caused internal damage (no power, no display, port fault) we diagnose and quote the functional repair. Cosmetic body work is separate. Does MacBook Air M2 support eGPU? No — eGPU support was removed from macOS Ventura. The M2 MacBook Air cannot use external GPUs regardless of macOS version. For the vast majority of faults yes. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Common questions MacBook Air M3 Repair — FAQ Can the RAM or SSD be upgraded on the MacBook Air M3? No. Both the Unified Memory (RAM) and SSD storage are integrated into the M3 Apple Silicon chip package on the A3113 and A3114. Neither can be upgraded after purchase. Configure with sufficient RAM and storage at point of purchase. My MacBook Air M3 gets hot during heavy use — is that normal? The MacBook Air M3 is completely fanless. It manages heat entirely through its aluminium chassis. Under sustained heavy loads (video export, compilation) it will throttle performance to manage temperature — this is by design. If the machine is hot during light tasks like web browsing, bring it in for a diagnostic. Can you recover data from an M3 MacBook Air with a failed logic board? M-series data recovery requires logic board restoration — storage is integrated into the chip and cannot be read independently. iAssist restores the board to a bootable state, then clones the data before proceeding with any repair. My MacBook Air M3 MagSafe port is not charging — what should I try first? Try a different MagSafe 3 cable. Also try charging via USB-C on one of the Thunderbolt ports to determine if the fault is MagSafe-specific or board-level. If neither charges, bring it in for a free diagnostic. How is the MacBook Air M3 different from the M2 for repairs? The M3 and M2 MacBook Air are very similar in design and repairability. The M3 uses Wi-Fi 6E versus the M2's Wi-Fi 6. Display assemblies differ between the 13-inch (A3113) and 15-inch (A3114). Battery is the same A2669 unit. Logic board repairs require M3-specific tooling and knowledge. Does the MacBook Air M3 have a fan? No — the MacBook Air has been fanless since the M1 in 2020. All M-series MacBook Air models use passive cooling through the aluminium body. There is no fan to service or replace. Can the MacBook Air M3 run Windows? Not natively. Apple Silicon does not support Boot Camp. Windows can be run in a virtual machine (Parallels, VMware Fusion) under macOS. We can assist with virtual machine setup if needed. My MacBook Air M3 won't turn on — what should I do? Hold the power button for 10 seconds to force a shutdown, then press once to restart. If still unresponsive, try connecting to power for 30 minutes then attempt startup. If it remains dead, bring it in for a free diagnostic — board-level power issues are diagnosable and often repairable. Do you offer collection for MacBook Air M3 repair? For most users yes — the M3 MacBook Air is an excellent machine that warrants repair for most faults including screen replacement. Apple officially dropped support for 2013–2017 MacBook Airs from Sonoma, but OCLP patches the installer to run it anyway. iAssist installs and configures OCLP for R1,500. An SSD upgrade at the same time gives the best experience. What is OpenCore Legacy Patcher? OCLP is a mature, widely-used open-source tool that patches macOS to run on Macs Apple no longer officially supports. For A1466 MacBook Air owners this means running Sonoma on a machine that would otherwise be stuck on Monterey. Millions of Macs worldwide run on OCLP-patched Sonoma daily. Which MacBook Air models can run Sonoma natively? MacBook Air 2018 (A1932) and newer run Sonoma natively. Older models — 2013–2017 A1466 and 11-inch A1465 — require OCLP for Sonoma. Is OCLP stable for daily use? Yes. OCLP is a mature project. For everyday use — web browsing, email, Office, media — it is completely stable. There are minor limitations with some GPU acceleration features but these do not affect typical use. Do I need an SSD before installing OCLP? Not required, but strongly recommended. All MacBook Airs already have SSDs. However if the drive is old, small, or slow, upgrading it before the OCLP install gives the best Sonoma experience. Will OCLP break when Apple releases new macOS? OCLP is updated with each major macOS release. When Apple releases macOS 16, OCLP releases a compatible version. iAssist can update your OCLP installation when new versions arrive. MacBook Air battery lifespan guide Apple's MacBook Air batteries are designed to retain 80% of original capacity through 1000 complete charge cycles. In real-world South African conditions — load-shedding, daily heavy use, ambient heat — replacement is often warranted earlier than that ceiling suggests. macOS will throttle processor performance once battery health drops below 80%, so a fresh battery often restores noticeable speed as well as runtime. Apple Silicon M1 · M2 · M3 · M4 · M5 500 Cycles · Monitor 800 Cycles · Replace Typical lifespan: 6–9 years. Apple Silicon batteries are the most durable Apple has shipped on the MacBook Air. At 500 cycles, monitor capacity. By 800 cycles or below 80% health, replacement restores both runtime and full processor speed. Intel · 2018–2020 Retina A1932 / A2179 300 Cycles · Monitor 500 Cycles · Replace Typical lifespan: 4–6 years. Battery part A1965. Intel Air batteries degrade faster than Apple Silicon under processor load. Below 80% capacity, expect noticeable performance loss especially during video calls and multitasking. Intel · 2013–2017 A1466 13-inch 250 Cycles · Monitor 400 Cycles · Replace Typical lifespan: 5–7 years. Battery part A1496. Battery-related shutdowns and unreliable runtime are common above 350 cycles. A fresh battery often transforms a 2013-2017 Air back into a dependable daily machine. Intel · 2010–2015 11-inch A1370 / A1465 10+ Years old Any Swelling · Replace Vintage territory. Battery parts A1406 (2010-2011) and A1495 (2012-2015). Original batteries are well past their service life. Replace any visibly swollen battery immediately — swollen cells can lift and damage the trackpad and topcase. Check your cycle count: Apple menu → About This Mac → More Info → System Report → Power . WhatsApp 078 742 4769 with your model and cycle count for a battery replacement quote — confirmed in writing before any work begins. Known MacBook Air issues Every MacBook Air generation eventually develops a personality — usually expressed through a specific design fault that turns up like clockwork after a few years of use. Below are the ones we see most often on the workshop bench. None is terminal. Each has a well-defined repair path and we've handled all of them many times over. MacBook Air M1 · A2337 CD3217B12 USB-C controller failure The M1 MacBook Air logic board uses two CD3217B12 USB-C power-delivery controller chips — one per port. These chips are a well-documented failure point: a power surge, a faulty third-party charger, or sometimes spontaneous component death can take one or both out. When they fail, the MacBook stops charging and refuses to power on. On a USB-C meter the board typically reads 5V with zero current draw. Apple's standard repair path is a full logic board replacement. On an M-series machine that means swapping out the entire computer — chip, RAM, and SSD storage included — which is extremely expensive and wipes your data with it. iAssist fix: Component-level replacement of the failed CD3217B12 chip(s) via micro-soldering. Original board preserved, all data on the integrated SSD kept intact, full charging and power restored at a fraction of the board-swap cost. MacBook Air 2018–2019 · A1932 Butterfly keyboard failure The 2018 and 2019 Intel MacBook Air used Apple's controversial butterfly mechanism keyboard. The shallow-travel design is prone to key bounce, sticky keys, double-letter input and complete switch failure from even tiny amounts of debris finding their way under the keycaps. Apple's keyboard service programme has now ended, so out-of-warranty butterfly failures need third-party repair. The 2020 A2179 returned to the reliable Magic Keyboard and is not affected. iAssist fix: Full topcase assembly replacement (keyboard, battery and chassis as one part). Permanent resolution under our standard repair warranty. MacBook Air 2018–2020 · A1932 / A2179 Thermal design causing CPU degradation & death Apple's thermal design on the 2018-2020 Intel MacBook Air is genuinely flawed — the cooling fan inside the chassis is not physically connected to the CPU heatsink. The fan circulates air around the inside of the case but doesn't directly cool the processor. Under sustained load — video calls, browser-heavy workflows, even macOS updates — CPU temperatures climb high enough to trigger aggressive thermal throttling, and over time, permanent CPU degradation. Many of these machines arrive with a dead or partially-dead CPU after years of compounding heat stress. Symptoms include sudden shutdowns under load, refusal to boot, GPU artefacts, or complete no-power faults. iAssist fix: Thermal paste service and thermal-pad modification can drop CPU temps by 20-30°C and prevent further degradation on healthy boards. For boards where the CPU has already failed, component-level board repair restores the machine where possible. All Retina MacBook Air models Anti-reflective coating delamination On all Retina-display MacBook Airs (2018 onwards), the anti-reflective coating applied to the display surface can react with skin oils, alcohol-based wipes, or trapped moisture and produce visible blotches, streaks or cloudy patches. The damage is permanent and cannot be cleaned off — sometimes called "Staingate" in user forums. Apple's coating repair programme covered earlier MacBook Pro models but not the MacBook Air. Out-of-warranty owners need third-party display work. iAssist fix: Full display assembly replacement using a colour-matched panel. Resolves the coating issue permanently and restores original display clarity. MacBook Air 2013–2017 · A1466 Trackpad-gap liquid ingress The 2013-2017 A1466 has a design quirk that makes even tiny spills disproportionately dangerous: the narrow gap at the top edge of the trackpad sits directly above the trackpad cable connector and a section of the logic board. The keyboard's plastic backlight sheet provides only limited protection — it's not water-tight. The result: just a few drops of water, a small coffee splash, or a knocked-over wine glass can seep through that gap and reach the board. Owners regularly report "barely anything spilled" and we open the machine to find significant corrosion on the trackpad cable connector and logic board. iAssist fix: Ultrasonic board cleaning, corrosion removal, trackpad cable replacement, and component-level repair of any damaged ICs. Bring it in immediately — corrosion continues spreading for days after a spill, even on a powered-off machine. MacBook Air 2018–2020 (Intel) · M1 onwards T2 / Apple Silicon data binding The 2018-2020 Intel MacBook Air introduced Apple's T2 Security Chip, and every M-series Air (M1 onwards) continued the model — all SSD storage is encrypted with keys tied to that specific logic board. If the board fails, the storage cannot be moved to another machine for data recovery. Many repair shops declare these machines unrecoverable. They aren't — the original board has to be restored to a bootable state first, then the data cloned, then the repair completed. iAssist fix: Component-level board restoration via micro-soldering, then data clone, then full repair. Data is always secured before any other repair work begins. Free MacBook Air diagnostics on all models. Written fixed-price quote before any work begins. No hidden fees. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Common questions MacBook Air Screen Repair — questions we get asked My MacBook Air screen is cracked but still works — should I still repair it? Yes — a cracked screen on a MacBook Air is a progressive problem. The LCD beneath the glass is exposed to further damage, debris can work into the cracks, and the structural integrity of the display is compromised. More importantly, a cracked screen on an M-series MacBook Air can damage the keyboard below it when the lid is closed. Repair is strongly advised before the damage worsens. Can just the glass be replaced on my MacBook Air, or does the whole display need replacing? On MacBook Air 2013–2017 models (A1466/A1465), the glass and LCD are separate — a glass-only replacement is possible if the LCD is undamaged. On 2018 and later models including all M-series, the glass and LCD are fully laminated and must be replaced as a complete display assembly. Free diagnostic confirms which applies to your machine. My MacBook Air screen has a pink or green tint in one corner — what is that? A localised colour tint on any MacBook Air display is almost always a display cable pressure fault or early panel delamination. It will not resolve itself and typically worsens over time. Bring it in for a free diagnostic — in many cases this is a cable seating issue resolved without a full panel replacement. My MacBook Air shows a white or black screen but still plays sound — is the display faulty? A no-image but active audio scenario on MacBook Air points to either a display cable fault, a failed backlight driver, or a GPU signal issue on the logic board. An external monitor test narrows this down immediately — if an external display works, the fault is in the display assembly or cable. Free diagnostic to confirm. How much does MacBook Air screen repair cost? Prices vary significantly by model year. The 2013–2017 models use a 1440×900 non-Retina panel that is relatively affordable to replace. The 2018–2020 Retina laminated assemblies are more expensive. M-series displays are the most expensive due to the integrated display architecture. Prices confirmed after the free diagnostic. Does screen replacement on MacBook Air affect Face ID or Touch ID? MacBook Air does not have Face ID. Touch ID on 2018 and later models is in the keyboard, not the display — screen replacement does not affect Touch ID function. How long does MacBook Air screen repair take? Most screen replacements are completed within 24–48 hours. We call you when ready. Same-day may be possible for some models — ask when you drop off. Do you offer collection for MacBook Air screen repair? Yes — R300 insured door-to-door collection and return across Gauteng. WhatsApp us on 078 742 4769. Can a MacBook Air screen be repaired if the hinge is also broken? Yes — we repair both the display and the hinge mechanism. Hinge repair is typically done alongside screen replacement to avoid opening the machine twice. Mention the hinge when you drop off. My MacBook Air has backlight bleed around the edges — is that normal? Mild uniformity variation is common on laptop displays. Significant backlight bleeding or bright spots around edges indicate a failing backlight diffuser or pressure on the panel. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Frequently asked questions MacBook Air speaker repair — questions we get asked How do I know if it's the speaker or the logic board? The clearest test: if only one speaker crackles and the other is fine, it's almost certainly the speaker itself. If both speakers fail at the same time — especially after a spill — the fault is more likely the audio IC on the logic board. iAssist diagnoses at component level before quoting. Depending on the cause, the fix is either speaker replacement or component-level IC repair on the logic board. Free diagnostic to confirm which before quoting. My MacBook Air has no sound after a spill — is it fixable? Very likely yes. Liquid damage to the speaker circuit is repairable in most cases. The speaker itself may need replacement, or the audio IC on the board needs replacement. Component-level repair, not a board swap. Bring it in immediately — dried liquid makes recovery harder. Does speaker replacement affect sound quality? iAssist uses OEM-grade replacement speakers matched to your model. Sound quality is restored to original specification. Can just the left or right speaker be replaced? Yes — individual speakers are replaced. There is no requirement to replace both unless both are faulty. What is the audio IC on a MacBook Air? When it fails — often from liquid exposure — both speakers go silent or produce severe distortion. It is replaceable at component level without replacing the entire logic board. My MacBook Air sounds fine through headphones — is the speaker dead? Yes. If audio routes correctly through headphones but not internal speakers, the fault is isolated to the speaker circuit. Only the 2013–2017 models (A1466 13-inch and A1465 11-inch) have a proprietary PCIe SSD blade that can be replaced with a larger, faster drive. All MacBook Air models from 2018 onwards — including the 2018/2019 Intel Retina, 2020 Intel, M1, M2, and M3 — have SSDs soldered to the logic board and cannot be upgraded under any circumstances. My MacBook Air 2017 is slow — will an SSD upgrade help? If your 2017 MacBook Air shipped with a smaller or slower SSD, upgrading to a faster blade makes a noticeable improvement.
