WhatsApp to arrange courier → Common questions MacBook Air Trackpad Repair — questions we get asked My MacBook Air trackpad click has stopped working — can that be fixed? Yes. Trackpad click failure is usually caused by a swollen battery lifting the trackpad from below (most common cause), a failed Force Touch haptic mechanism (2015+ models), or a trackpad cable fault. A swollen battery is a safety issue and should be addressed urgently. Free diagnostic identifies the cause before quoting. The cursor on my MacBook Air jumps around randomly — what causes that? Cursor jumping is almost always caused by a trackpad calibration fault or a partially failed trackpad cable. It can also be caused by a swollen battery creating uneven pressure on the trackpad surface. On Intel models, an SMC reset (Intel: hold Shift+Control+Option+Power for 10 seconds) sometimes resolves firmware-level trackpad glitches. My MacBook Air trackpad is unresponsive but the keyboard works fine — is it the trackpad or logic board? If the keyboard works but trackpad does not, the fault is almost certainly the trackpad cable or the trackpad unit itself — not the logic board. This is a far more manageable repair than a board-level fault. How much does MacBook Air trackpad repair cost? Trackpad cable replacement is relatively affordable. Trackpad unit replacement varies by model and is confirmed after the free diagnostic. If a swollen battery is causing the issue, battery replacement is done simultaneously. Does MacBook Air trackpad repair require replacing the whole topcase? On M-series models the trackpad is more integrated, but on most Intel models the trackpad can be replaced independently of the keyboard topcase. Free diagnostic confirms the scope before quoting. My MacBook Air trackpad makes a grinding noise when I click — what is that? A grinding trackpad click indicates debris in the mechanism or a failing click mechanism. On Force Touch models (2015+), this can also indicate a failed haptic actuator. Both are repairable. Free diagnostic to confirm. Can I disable the trackpad and use a mouse while waiting for repair? Yes — connect any USB or Bluetooth mouse. In System Settings → Accessibility → Pointer Control, you can enable 'Ignore built-in trackpad when mouse or wireless trackpad is present' to prevent the faulty trackpad from interfering. How long does MacBook Air trackpad repair take? Trackpad cable replacement: 1–2 hours. Trackpad unit replacement: 2–4 hours. Same-day turnaround is often possible. We confirm when you drop off. Do you offer collection for MacBook Air trackpad repair? Yes — R300 insured door-to-door collection across Gauteng. WhatsApp 078 742 4769. My MacBook Air trackpad stopped working after a macOS update — is that a software issue? Occasionally yes — a macOS update can cause trackpad firmware issues. Try an SMC reset first. If the trackpad remains unresponsive after a reset and system restart, the fault has a hardware component. When one fails — typically from a voltage spike, faulty cable, or heat — that port stops working entirely while the other remains functional. iAssist replaces the failed controller IC at component level under microscope. A2337 M1, A2179, A1932 all share this two-port architecture. USB device not recognised — external drive, hub, or dongle A partially failed Thunderbolt or USB-C controller can lose data capability while still passing power for charging. The drive spins up but never mounts, or the hub connects briefly then disconnects. Free diagnostic to confirm whether the fault is the port, the cable, the hub, or the controller IC. External display not detected — Thunderbolt fault Thunderbolt 3 display output routes through the Thunderbolt controller IC. A failed controller means the display is never detected — the Mac doesn't even see it as a connected device. Controller IC replacement restores full Thunderbolt 3 functionality. USB-C port physically damaged — bent or debris inside Forcing a connector, debris in the port, or a dropped machine can damage the port socket physically. The USB-C daughterboard is replaceable — socket damage is not a logic board replacement situation. Charging only works on one side The MacBook Air A1932, A2179, and A2337 can charge from either USB-C port. If charging only works on one side, the USB-C controller or the USB-C board on the dead side has failed. Board-level repair. CD3217B12 / CD3217B13 controller failure — completely dead machine The Texas Instruments CD3217 USB-C power delivery controller is responsible for negotiating charging and power delivery on A1932, A2179, and A2337 models. When it fails the machine is completely dead — no charging light, no power at all. Component-level IC replacement under microscope. Very common fault, high success rate. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Frequently asked questions MacBook Air USB-C and Thunderbolt — questions we get asked Why does only one USB-C port work on my MacBook Air? The two USB-C ports share a daughterboard but each has its own controller IC. When one controller fails — from voltage spike, heat, or faulty cable — only that port stops working. iAssist replaces the IC at component level without replacing the whole logic board. My external drive is not recognised but charging still works — what is wrong? Charging uses a simpler power path than data. A partially failed USB-C or Thunderbolt controller can lose data capability while still passing power. Free diagnostic to confirm before quoting. Is a dead USB-C port a logic board replacement? Not necessarily. In most cases the fault is the USB-C daughterboard or a controller IC — both replaceable at component level. iAssist diagnoses at component level before recommending a board replacement, which is always the last resort. My MacBook Air is completely dead and won't charge from either port — what is it? Very likely the CD3217B12 or CD3217B13 Texas Instruments USB-C power delivery controller IC. When it fails the machine is completely dead. This is a component-level repair, not a board replacement. Common fault on A1932, A2179, and A2337 models with a high success rate. Can you fix a physically broken USB-C port? Yes — a bent or damaged USB-C socket is replaced on the daughterboard. This is not a logic board repair. My Thunderbolt display is not detected — is this fixable? Yes in most cases. Thunderbolt display output routes through the Thunderbolt controller IC. A failed controller is replaced at component level. Free diagnostic to confirm. How long does USB-C port repair take? Most repairs are same-day or next-day depending on parts availability. CD3217 IC replacement typically takes 1–2 days. WhatsApp 078 742 4769 to confirm. Does USB-C repair affect the rest of my MacBook Air? USB-C daughterboard replacement from R900. Controller IC repair from R1,500. CD3217 replacement from R1,500. Free diagnostic and written quote before work begins. My MacBook Air charges slowly from one port but not the other — is this the same fault? Slow charging from one port while the other charges normally points to a failing controller IC on the slow port. The port can still negotiate lower wattage power delivery but has lost full Thunderbolt capability. https://iassist.net.za/pages/macbook-pro.text: id="MainContent" class="content-for-layout focus-none" role="main" tabindex="-1"> MacBook Pro Audio Jack & I/O Board Repair Johannesburg | iAssist Home → MacBook Pro Repairs → Audio Jack & I/O Board Repair 🎧 Headphone jack · Microphone · I/O board · Audio IC MacBook Pro Audio Jack & I/O Board Repair You plug in your headphones for a Teams call and get absolute silence. You unplug them and now the speakers are dead too. Welcome to MacBook Pro audio problems — where the 3.5mm jack, the audio codec IC, and the T1 or T2 chip can each fail independently and take each other down with them. Pre-2016 MacBook Pros (A1278, A1286, A1502, A1398) have a discrete I/O board where the jack physically lives — we replace the jack or swap the I/O board as a unit, keeping cost lower. From 2016 onwards Apple integrated audio into the logic board, so repair means microsoldering at the audio IC or jack assembly. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Frequently asked questions MacBook Pro audio jack & I/O board — questions we get asked Why has the audio jack on my MacBook Pro stopped working? The most common cause on Intel-era MacBook Pros (2012-2019) is corrosion or debris inside the jack itself — dust, sweat, hair, lint accumulate over years of headphone use. The second cause is the audio IC on the I/O board developing a cold solder joint or partial failure. On Touch Bar models the audio path runs through the T1/T2 chip, so a T-chip fault can also kill the headphone output. M-series MacBook Pros (M1 onwards) integrate audio routing directly into the SoC and connecting board — failures there are board-level repairs at component level. Do you replace the whole I/O board, or just the audio jack? Depends on the era. Pre-2016 MacBook Pros have a discrete I/O board where the audio jack physically lives, so we can either replace the jack itself or swap the I/O board if multiple components are damaged. Touch Bar era 2016-2019 partially integrated audio into the logic board — a discrete I/O board still exists for MagSafe/USB-C/audio on some sub-models but functionality is shared with the logic board. M-series 2020+ has heavy integration — audio repair is usually component-level on the logic board itself. My MacBook Pro plays sound but the microphone doesn't work — same fix? Often, yes. The internal microphone, headphone jack, and audio IC share the same audio bus on most MacBook Pros. A failure on the audio codec IC kills both. Liquid damage near the speakers or top case is another common cause — the mic capsules are usually right next to the speakers in the top case. We diagnose audio out and audio in together because the fix is usually the same component or trace. My headphones only work if I jiggle the jack — can that be fixed? Yes. Intermittent jack contact is almost always a mechanical issue: bent contacts inside the 3.5mm jack housing, corrosion on the pins, or a worn-out detection switch. On Intel Retina MacBook Pros we replace the jack itself (R1,400-R2,800). On Touch Bar models replacement is harder — the jack is integrated into the I/O board assembly so the whole sub-assembly may need replacing (R2,200-R4,500). On M-series the jack is part of the integrated audio sub-board, repair is component-level. How much does MacBook Pro audio jack or I/O board repair cost? Pre-2016 Intel MacBook Pros: R1,200-R2,800 for discrete jack or I/O board work. 2016-2019 Touch Bar era: R2,200-R4,500 — more complex due to T1/T2 integration. 2019-2020 16-inch and Apple Silicon M1/M2/M3/M4: R3,500-R8,500 for board-level component repair. All quotes are written and fixed before any work begins. Diagnostic is always free. Will my MacBook Pro speakers also need replacement? Not usually. The speakers and the audio jack are different components — speakers are physical drivers in the top case, the jack is on the I/O board. We see liquid damage that takes out both, but most jack failures don't affect speakers. If you have audio crackling or distortion from speakers alongside the jack issue, it's likely the audio amplifier IC failing — that's a board-level repair we can do at the same time. Is the MacBook Pro audio jack repairable on Apple Silicon (M1-M5)? Yes. While Apple integrates more components into the SoC and logic board on M-series MacBook Pros, the headphone jack itself is still a physical connector that lives on a sub-board. We can service it through component-level micro-soldering. The integrated audio routing means we sometimes need to repair traces on the main logic board too, but it's all repairable — Apple Silicon hasn't made these things unserviceable. Can liquid damage cause audio jack failure? Almost always. Liquid (especially sugary drinks or seawater) corrodes the audio IC and the contact pads inside the jack. On a MacBook Pro you'd typically see this paired with speaker distortion, microphone failure, and sometimes intermittent power. If you've spilled liquid and audio is affected: do not power on, get it to us within 24-48 hours for ultrasonic clean + corrosion remediation. The longer it sits, the more board traces corrode. Common battery problems MacBook Pro battery issues we fix Battery drains in under 2 hours Normal MacBook Pro battery life is 8–18 hours depending on model. A battery draining in 2 hours or less is failing. Check System Settings → Battery → Battery Health — below 80% warrants replacement. M-series batteries degrade more slowly than Intel models. MacBook Pro shuts down unexpectedly at 20–40% Sudden shutdowns at partial charge indicate a failing battery that can no longer deliver consistent current under load. The battery reads capacity incorrectly because cell chemistry has degraded. Battery replacement resolves this. Swollen battery — trackpad raised or lid won't close A visibly swollen battery is a fire risk. Stop using the machine immediately. On Intel MacBook Pros the swollen battery can crack the trackpad and bottom case. iAssist replaces swollen batteries as a priority repair. Do not puncture or compress a swollen battery. Won't charge — charger light on but battery stays at 0% If the charger indicator is on but battery percentage doesn't increase, the battery BMS (Battery Management System) has failed, or there is a charging circuit fault on the logic board. Battery replacement resolves most cases. Free diagnostic to confirm. Battery health at 0% or not detected System Information shows no battery or Service Recommended immediately after installation of a new macOS. Usually a dead battery or failed BMS chip. Battery replacement. macOS says "Service Recommended" or "Replace Now" When macOS displays Service Recommended or Replace Now under System Settings → Battery → Battery Health, the battery has degraded below 80% of its original capacity or the battery management system has flagged a fault. The machine will continue to work but performance and runtime are affected. Replace Now means Apple considers the battery a safety concern — act sooner rather than later. iAssist replaces batteries at any health status with a 6-month warranty. MacBook Pro running slow — battery causing CPU throttling A failing battery that can no longer deliver consistent current under load causes macOS to throttle the CPU to reduce power demand. This is called battery-related performance throttling and is separate from thermal throttling. Symptoms: the machine feels sluggish, fans spin up, and performance is inconsistent even when plugged in. A new battery restores full CPU performance immediately. If your MacBook Pro feels slow and the battery health is low — the battery is the first thing to replace. MacBook Pro won't turn on — dead battery A fully depleted or dead battery can prevent the MacBook Pro from turning on even with a charger connected. On some models the machine will not boot without a functional battery present — the charger alone is not enough. If your MacBook Pro shows no response at all, try holding the power button for 10 seconds, then connect the charger and wait 5 minutes before pressing power again. If it still won't turn on, bring it in — the battery may need replacement before the machine can boot. Fan grinding or rattling noise Bearing wear inside the fan causes grinding at certain RPMs. A failing fan bearing will eventually seize — leaving the machine with no active cooling. Fan running at full speed all the time Fan stuck at maximum RPM despite normal load usually indicates a failed temperature sensor or SMC fault. Fan replacement in most cases. MacBook Pro hot to the touch during normal use Chassis running hot during light use is usually dried or cracked thermal paste on older Intel models. Thermal paste replacement returns temperatures to normal operating range. Fan noise after liquid spill Liquid ingress into the fan housing degrades the bearing. Fan replacement after liquid damage rather than cleaning — contaminated bearings wear rapidly. Is it normal for MacBook Pro fans to run loudly during video export? Yes — sustained CPU/GPU workloads like video export spin the fans to full speed. This is normal thermal management. If fans run loudly during light tasks like web browsing, thermal paste replacement or a temperature sensor diagnosis is warranted. Can I use my MacBook Pro while the fan is grinding? Not for long. A failing fan bearing will seize. Once it seizes the machine has no active cooling and will thermally throttle to minimum performance within minutes of load. Fan replacement is urgent if the grinding is getting worse. How long does fan replacement take? Same-day if we have the specific fan in stock. Next-day if we need to order. WhatsApp 078 742 4769 to confirm availability for your model. Do 14/16-inch M-series MacBook Pros have one or two fans? 14-inch M-series has one fan. 16-inch M-series has two fans. Both also have large heat spreaders compared to the 13-inch fanless MacBook Pro. How much does MacBook Pro fan replacement cost? Varies by model. Single fan or dual fan replacement confirmed before booking. Free diagnostic to confirm the fan is the fault before quoting. Can thermal service improve battery life? Yes — a CPU running cooler draws less power, which improves battery life on Intel models. M-series models already run efficiently but thermal paste replacement after 5+ years can modestly improve battery run time. What warranty does thermal service carry? 6-month warranty on all fan replacements. Apple's butterfly mechanism uses an extremely thin key travel design that is highly susceptible to dust and debris. A single particle under the key mechanism stops the switch registering. Apple ran a free repair programme which has since ended. The 2019 13-inch and 2019 16-inch switched back to the scissor mechanism. Does topcase replacement fix all butterfly keyboard problems? Yes — topcase replacement replaces the entire keyboard, trackpad, battery, and palm rest as a single unit. It resolves all butterfly keyboard mechanical failures permanently. Will Touch ID work after topcase replacement on M-series? Touch ID on M-series MacBook Pros is cryptographically paired to the Secure Enclave on the logic board. Topcase replacement requires Apple Configurator re-pairing to restore fingerprint authentication. iAssist advises this before any topcase work. Can individual keys be replaced on a MacBook Pro? On 2019-onwards models with scissor mechanisms yes — individual keycaps and mechanisms can be replaced. On 2016–2019 butterfly keyboard models, Apple's design makes individual key replacement impractical — topcase replacement is the correct repair. My Touch Bar is not working — is this a keyboard repair? The Touch Bar has its own dedicated page and repair path. It's a separate display strip with its own controller — not part of the keyboard mechanism. See our Touch Bar repair page. How long does MacBook Pro keyboard repair take? Topcase replacement is typically same-day or next-day depending on parts availability. WhatsApp 078 742 4769 to confirm. My 2019 MacBook Pro keys feel sticky after a spill — do I need a new topcase? Free diagnostic to confirm. What is the difference between the butterfly and scissor keyboard? The butterfly mechanism (2016–2019) uses a single butterfly-shaped pivot under each key with 0.5mm travel. The scissor mechanism (2019-onwards) uses a standard scissor switch with 1mm travel and is far more reliable and comfortable. Is MacBook Pro keyboard repair covered by AppleCare? Switch off immediately — hold the power button. Unplug the charger. Turn it upside down to drain. Do not use a hair dryer. Do not put it in rice — rice does nothing for corrosion. Bring it in as soon as possible. My MacBook Pro still works after the spill — do I still need to bring it in? Yes. A machine that works after a spill is developing corrosion on the logic board right now. Corrosion from a water-based spill spreads over hours and days. Early intervention limits the damage to one or two components. Waiting results in multiple component failures. Can a liquid-damaged MacBook Pro always be repaired? Most can, especially if brought in quickly. A machine that died immediately from a coffee spill is often repairable — it's a short circuit, not physical destruction. A machine that sat powered on while corroding for a week is harder. Bring it in immediately for the best outcome. Is rice actually helpful after a laptop spill? No. Rice absorbs some surface moisture but does nothing to prevent or reverse corrosion on the logic board. Time spent in rice is time corrosion is spreading. Bring it in immediately. Far fewer have the microscope, the hot-air rework station, the schematics — or the years of practice it takes to actually repair a logic board. Here's what that means in practice. Diagnosis under a microscope Most shops eyeball the board. We examine every MacBook Pro under a stereo microscope, tracing power rails and identifying the specific failed component — a single capacitor, a chip, a corroded trace — rather than blaming the whole board. The failed part named in your quote Your written quote tells you exactly which component has failed. "Board fault" isn't a diagnosis — "CD3217B12 USB-C controller, port 2" is. You agree to fix a real fault, not a vague verdict. We repair the part, not the board Micro-soldering replaces the failed chip or trace and leaves the rest of the board — your SSD, your data, your installed apps — exactly where they were. Full board swaps wipe everything. We don't, where it can be avoided. Honest verdicts, including "walk away" When a repair doesn't make sense — a 2011 board with multiple faults, a screen swap on a machine worth less than the part — we say so before any work begins. No padding the bill. No selling you a fix you don't need. MacBook Pro battery lifespan guide Apple's MacBook Pro batteries are designed to retain 80% of original capacity through 1000 complete charge cycles. In real-world South African conditions — load-shedding, sustained workloads, ambient heat — replacement is often warranted earlier than that ceiling suggests. macOS will throttle processor performance once battery health drops below 80%, so a fresh battery often restores noticeable speed as well as runtime. Apple Silicon M1 · M2 · M3 · M4 · M5 500 Cycles · Monitor 800 Cycles · Replace Typical lifespan: 5–8 years. Apple Silicon MacBook Pros (A2289, A2338, A2442, A2485, A2779, A2780, A2918, A2992, A2991, A3293, A3294, A3295) ship with the most durable batteries Apple has shipped on the MBP. Battery parts A2389, A2519, A2527 depending on chassis. At 500 cycles monitor capacity. By 800 cycles or below 80% health, replacement restores both runtime and full processor speed. Intel · 2019–2020 16-inch & 13-inch four-port 300 Cycles · Monitor 500 Cycles · Replace Typical lifespan: 4–6 years. Battery parts A2113 (A2141 16-inch 2019), A2171 (A2251/A2289 13-inch 2020). Intel MBPs degrade faster than Apple Silicon under heavy workloads. Below 80% capacity expect noticeable performance loss especially during video calls, Final Cut renders, and multitasking. Intel · 2016–2019 Touch Bar 13-inch & 15-inch Touch Bar 300 Cycles · Monitor 500 Cycles · Replace Typical lifespan: 4–6 years. Battery parts A1819 (A1706/A1708 13-inch 2016-2017), A1820 (A1707 15-inch 2016-2017), A1953 (A1990 15-inch 2018-2019), A1964 (A1989 13-inch 2018-2019). Battery health drops faster on Touch Bar models due to thermals — these models share their battery cavity with hot CPUs. Intel · 2012–2015 Retina 13-inch & 15-inch Retina 300 Cycles · Monitor 400 Cycles · Replace Typical lifespan: 5–7 years. Battery parts A1437 (A1425 13-inch 2012-2013), A1493 (A1502 13-inch 2013-2015), A1417 (A1398 15-inch 2012-2013), A1494 (A1398 15-inch 2013-2015). Known MacBook Pro issues Each MacBook Pro generation has known design faults that develop over years of use. The most common issues we repair are listed below. All are well-documented and have established repair paths. 2016-2017 · 13-inch + 15-inch Touch Bar Flexgate The display backlight ribbon cable was made too short, causing it to flex tightly every time the lid opens and closes. After enough cycles the cable cracks. Affects both 13-inch (A1706 / A1708) and 15-inch (A1707) 2016-2017 models. Symptoms: stage-light effect at the bottom of the screen, backlight failing on one side, complete backlight loss. Apple ran a quality program for the 2016 13-inch that has now expired for most; the 15-inch was never covered. We replace the flex cable as a board-level repair on both sizes. Fix: Display flex cable replacement · R2,800–R4,500 2015-2019 · 13" & 15" Touch Bar Butterfly keyboard failure The butterfly-mechanism keyboard introduced in 2015 (1st gen) and refined through 2019 (4th gen) developed a notorious reliability problem. Single particles of dust or crumbs can cause keys to stick, double-register, or stop responding entirely. Apple's Keyboard Service Program covered specific affected models — most have now exited that window. Symptoms: sticky keys, dead keys, double letters, unresponsive space bar. Fix: Full top case replacement · R3,500–R8,500 2018-2020 · Touch Bar T2 T2 chip power management The T2 security chip introduced on 2018 MacBook Pros handles SSD encryption, audio, image signal processing, and power management. T2 firmware bugs and hardware quirks cause random shutdowns, kernel panics, and "battery not charging" warnings even with healthy batteries. Symptoms: random power-off mid-task, refusal to boot after sleep, charging halting at random percentages. Fix: T2 reset, SMC reset, or board-level repair · R1,500–R6,500 2011-2013 · 15-inch Retina Discrete GPU (dGPU) failure The 2011-2013 15-inch MacBook Pros with discrete AMD Radeon graphics developed a well-documented failure pattern — the GPU package's solder fails under thermal cycling. Symptoms: black screen on boot, vertical lines, distorted graphics, kernel panic, repeated reboots into safe mode. Apple's Repair Extension Program ended years ago. The fix is to disable the dGPU via terminal and run on integrated graphics — or full GPU reflow / replacement. Fix: dGPU disable or replacement · R1,200–R6,500 2013-2015 · Retina 13" & 15" Staingate (AR coating delamination) The 2013-2015 Retina screens used an anti-reflective coating that delaminates with cleaning, screen wipes, or even cloth pressure. Apple ran a Display Replacement Program that has now ended. Symptoms: blotchy white patches on the screen, particularly around the trackpad area. The screen still functions, but the coating blotches are visually disruptive. We can either polish off remaining AR coating (R650) or replace the LCD assembly. Fix: AR coating polish or LCD swap · R650–R6,500 All Touch Bar models 2016-2019 Backlight fuse failure A small fuse on the logic board controls the LED backlight. Vibration, surges, or liquid intrusion can blow this fuse. Symptoms: screen appears completely dark — but if you shine a torch at the display, you can see the image is still there. The LCD is fine, just no backlight power. Component-level board repair restores backlight. Fix: Backlight fuse / circuit repair · R1,500–R3,500 Free MacBook Pro diagnostics on all models. WhatsApp to arrange courier → Frequently asked questions MacBook Pro screen repair — questions we get asked How much does MacBook Pro screen repair cost? Display assemblies vary significantly by model, chip variant, and colour. ProMotion 14/16-inch assemblies are more expensive than 13-inch Retina panels. iAssist confirms pricing before booking. Free diagnostic to identify the exact assembly required. Can a MacBook Pro screen be repaired without replacing the whole assembly? On M-series and Retina Intel models the display assembly is a sealed unit — panel, glass, and backlight cannot be separated. On non-Retina 2008–2012 models the glass and LCD can be replaced independently. Board-level backlight repair is possible on all models without replacing the display. What is Staingate on a MacBook Pro? Staingate is the delamination of the anti-reflective coating on 2012–2015 Retina MacBook Pros. It appears as cloudy, oily patches across the display. Display assembly replacement resolves it permanently. Apple's free programme has ended. My MacBook Pro has purple lines on the display — is it the screen or the cable? Purple or coloured vertical lines are most commonly caused by a strained display cable in the hinge on 2016–2019 models. Free diagnostic to confirm whether cable replacement or full assembly is needed. Does MacBook Pro screen repair affect Touch ID? No. Touch ID on MacBook Pro is in the keyboard or the power button — not the display assembly. Screen repair does not affect Touch ID. How long does MacBook Pro screen repair take? Same-day or next-day depending on parts availability. ProMotion 14/16-inch assemblies may take 1–2 days to source. WhatsApp 078 742 4769 to confirm. My MacBook Pro screen goes black when I open the lid past a certain angle — what is this? Classic display cable strain fault on 2016 models. The cable cracks at the hinge point from years of opening and closing. Display assembly replacement resolves it completely. Can you fix a MacBook Pro with no display at all? Yes — a black screen with the machine otherwise running is typically a cable, connector, or GPU fault. iAssist diagnoses at component level before recommending a repair path. Is ProMotion 120Hz display replacement available? Yes. iAssist sources ProMotion Liquid Retina XDR assemblies for M-series 14 and 16-inch MacBook Pros. Prices confirmed before booking. Will screen replacement affect my warranty? Touch Bar is on: Intel 13-inch 2016–2020 (A1706, A1708, A1989, A2251, A2289), Intel 15-inch 2016–2019 (A1707, A1990), Intel 16-inch 2019–2020 (A2141), M1 13-inch 2020–2022 (A2338), and M2 13-inch 2022 (A2338). M1 Pro/Max, M2 Pro/Max, M3, and M4 MacBook Pros use physical function keys — no Touch Bar. My Touch Bar is black — is it broken? First try an SMC reset: Shift+Control+Option+Power held for 10 seconds. This resolves software-related black Touch Bar in many cases. If it remains black after reset, the Touch Bar assembly or controller has failed and hardware repair is required. Can the Touch Bar be repaired or does it need replacing? The Touch Bar OLED strip is not repairable at component level — replacement is the standard fix. The Touch Bar flex cable can be replaced independently if the strip itself is working but intermittently disconnecting. My Touch ID is in the Touch Bar and it stopped working — what happens after Touch Bar replacement? Touch ID in the Touch Bar is linked to the T1/T2 security chip. On Intel models, Touch Bar replacement does not break Touch ID pairing — the sensor remains paired to the machine. iAssist tests Touch ID functionality after every Touch Bar replacement. Is the Touch Bar worth repairing? On a machine you otherwise depend on, yes. The Touch Bar provides app-specific shortcuts, emoji input, and Touch ID. A black or dead Touch Bar is functionally annoying. Assessment + quote approach means you know the cost before committing. How long does Touch Bar repair take? Touch Bar replacement is typically same-day or next-day. WhatsApp 078 742 4769 to confirm parts availability for your specific model. My Touch Bar shows lines or dead zones — is this the cable or the strip? Visible lines or dead zones on the Touch Bar OLED strip indicate the strip itself has failed — not the cable. Touch Bar assembly replacement resolves this. Can a Touch Bar failure cause the keyboard to stop working? No. The Touch Bar and keyboard are separate components on the topcase. A Touch Bar failure does not affect keyboard functionality. Is Touch Bar repair covered by AppleCare? If in AppleCare period, Apple covers Touch Bar repair. Out of AppleCare, iAssist performs Touch Bar repair at competitive rates with a 6-month warranty. Do new MacBook Pros still have a Touch Bar? No. Apple removed the Touch Bar with the M1 Pro/Max 14/16-inch in 2021 and the M2 Pro/Max in 2023. All current MacBook Pros use physical function keys. We repair all MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models ever released — from older Intel generations including 2011 and 2012 Retina models all the way through to the latest M4 Pro and M4 Max. This includes MacBook Air M1, M2, and M3, MacBook Pro M2, M3, and M4 in both 14-inch and 16-inch configurations, and all Intel MacBook models from 2016 through 2020. If your model is not listed simply WhatsApp us — we have not turned a MacBook away yet. How much does MacBook screen repair cost in South Africa? MacBook screen replacement at iAssist costs between R2,500 and R12,000 depending on your model and screen size. Older Intel MacBook Air and Pro screens sit toward the lower end while newer Liquid XDR ProMotion displays on MacBook Pro M3 and M4 models carry a premium. Can you repair MacBook liquid damage? Yes — do not attempt to turn on a liquid-damaged MacBook as this causes further short-circuit damage. Bring it in as soon as possible. We use ultrasonic cleaning and component-level board repair to recover liquid-damaged MacBooks with a 90% success rate. Your data stays completely safe throughout the process. The sooner the device is treated the better the outcome — ideally within 24 hours of exposure. Can you repair M1, M2, M3 and M4 MacBook logic boards? Yes — and this is where iAssist stands apart from most repair centres in South Africa. Apple Silicon logic board repairs require chip-level micro-soldering expertise that most shops do not have and therefore turn away. Our technicians are trained in component-level board repair, meaning we diagnose and fix faults at chip level rather than replacing the entire board. This is significantly cheaper than an Apple out-of-warranty replacement and your data remains completely intact throughout. My MacBook is running very hot and the fan is constantly at full speed — can you fix it? Yes — this is one of the most common MacBook issues we see, particularly on Intel models. The cause is almost always dried-out thermal paste on the CPU and GPU combined with dust buildup in the cooling system. We fully disassemble the MacBook, clean the heatsink and fan, apply fresh premium thermal paste, and test under load before returning it. Most customers notice an immediate and significant improvement in temperature, fan noise, and overall performance after this service. Can you fix MacBook Flexgate backlight failure? Yes — Flexgate is a known design fault affecting MacBook Pro models from 2016 to 2018 where the backlight flex cable wears out over time causing a stage-light effect at the bottom of the screen or a complete backlight failure. We repair this at component level rather than replacing the entire display assembly, which significantly reduces the cost. If your MacBook screen dims at the bottom or goes dark when you open the lid past a certain angle, this is almost certainly Flexgate. Do you replace MacBook batteries? Yes — we replace MacBook batteries on all models using OEM-grade cells. If your MacBook is showing a Service Recommended battery warning, draining rapidly, shutting down unexpectedly at higher percentages, or has a swollen battery lifting the trackpad, a battery replacement is almost always the fix. Battery replacement costs between R1,500 and R4,000 depending on your model and most are completed the same day. Can you upgrade my MacBook SSD or RAM? SSD and RAM upgrades are available on older Intel MacBook models where the hardware allows it. On Apple Silicon MacBooks the RAM and SSD are integrated into the M-series chip and cannot be upgraded after purchase. However if your Apple Silicon MacBook has performance or storage issues we can diagnose whether a software, thermal, or board-level fix is possible. HDMI port replacement starts from R1,500 on both the Series X and Series S. If the HDMI retimer chip has also failed, chip replacement starts from R1,800. You get the exact price in writing after a free diagnostic, before any work starts. How do I know if it's the HDMI port or the retimer chip? A port fault usually follows physical damage: the console was knocked over or carried with the cable in, the plug feels loose, or the pins look bent. A retimer fault usually follows a power surge, and the port looks perfect. We check both under the microscope before quoting, so you only pay for the part that's failed. My Xbox turns on but there's no picture. Is it the HDMI port? Very often, yes. First try another HDMI cable, another TV input and the display reset (Xbox + Eject from off; Series S: Xbox + Pair). If there's still no picture, the HDMI port or the retimer chip is the most likely cause. What is the HDMI retimer chip? It's a small chip between the Xbox's processor and its HDMI port that cleans up the high-speed 4K signal before it reaches your TV. When it fails, the console powers on normally and the port can look perfect, but the TV gets no signal. Can a damaged HDMI cable cause this? Yes. A cable with a bent plug or broken wires can cause flicker or no signal, and a bent plug can damage the port. Always try another cable first, and bring yours in so we can check it. Will I lose my games and saves? No. An HDMI repair doesn't touch the storage, so your games, saves and settings stay as they are. Xbox saves also sync to the cloud when the console is online. How long does an Xbox HDMI repair take? Most repairs are done within 3–5 working days after you approve the quote, including a test at 4K with a game running. Retimer chip repairs and rescues of previous repairs can take longer, and we'll tell you upfront. How do I stop it happening again? Never move or carry the console with the HDMI cable plugged in, stand the Series X where it can't be knocked over, leave some slack in the cable, and plug the console into a surge protector to protect the retimer chip.
